literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 所谓旧世界汉坦病毒,与HFRS相关,主要分布在亚洲、欧洲以及非洲部分地区。相比之下,新世界汉坦病毒,导致HPS,主要局限于北美洲和南美洲。每年全球约有150000-200000例HFRS病例需要住院治疗,其中最大的负担出现在发展中国家。HFRS的死亡率范围从低于1%到约12%,具体取决于感染的病毒株。这两种疾病形式均以毛细血管通透性增加为特征,导致临床表现如低血压、血小板减少和白细胞增多。此外,新病毒株的发现以及报告病例的持续上升已加剧了全球对汉坦病毒的关注。 [10.5501/wjv.120334]
中国表明,持续的监测、储存宿主监测、基于风险的疫苗接种、啮齿动物控制和环境风险降低可以显著减少疾病负担,但发病率的下降并不意味着生态风险的消失。其双HTNV和SEOV生态进一步表明,一种临床综合征可能源于不同的农业和家庭周边啮齿动物相关接口。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2721722]
Cluster I中的HFRS病例表现出最高的临床严重程度(22.41%严重,6.65%危重),而Cluster II中的病例则明显较轻(2.62%严重,1.31%危重)。发病至就诊间隔的中位数在Cluster II中最长(5天),而其他区域为2-4天。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014746]
年龄、Calodium hepaticum疤痕、伤口、堆积物、开放排污沟渠和未铺装土壤与莱普托斯珀里拉阳性率呈正相关。年龄和堆积物的存在与汉坦病毒阳性率呈正相关,而鼠类控制活动和雄性特征则具有保护作用。 [10.1007/s10393-026-01836-z]
综述的文献显示,炎症细胞因子(IL-6、IL-18、CXCL10、CX3CL1)升高,与IRE1α依赖性焦亡相关的黏膜相关不变T(MAIT)细胞减少,内皮细胞糖萼的破坏,以及凝血功能障碍与血小板功能障碍。糖萼损伤的生物标志物(肝素硫酸盐、硫酸软骨素和可溶性血栓调节蛋白)与增加的死亡率风险相关(AUC 0.87–0.93)。 [10.1186/s40001-026-05202-1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The so-called old world hantaviruses, which are associated with HFRS, are predominantly distributed across Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa. In contrast, new world hantaviruses, responsible for HPS, are largely confined to North and South America. [10.5501/wjv.120334]

China demonstrates that sustained surveillance, reservoir monitoring, risk-defined vaccination, rodent control and environmental risk reduction can substantially reduce disease burden, but declining incidence does not mean disappearance of ecological risk. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2721722]

HFRS cases in Cluster I exhibited the highest clinical severity (22.41% severe, 6.65% critical), while cases in Cluster II were strikingly mild (2.62% severe, 1.31% critical). Median onset-to-visit interval was longest in Cluster II (5 days) vs others (2-4 days). [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014746]
Age, presence of Calodium hepaticum scars, wounds, accumulated materials, open sewer canals, and unpaved soil were positively associated with Leptospira positivity. [10.1007/s10393-026-01836-z]

Overall, 27.3% of patients with HFRS-AKI progressed to CKD despite receiving supportive care. Multivariate analysis revealed that treatment with Cordyceps sinensis preparations during the AKI phase was an independent protective factor against incomplete kidney recovery (OR: 0.323, 95% CI: 0.114-0.916, p = 0.034). [10.1080/0886022x.2026.2728349]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: PAHO主任强调了实验室准备在应对健康威胁中的重要性,以汉坦病毒为例说明整合系统对于有效公共卫生行动至关重要。 [news-4558c5b2cb403687]
一项题为“汉坦病毒感染中血管渗漏的免疫发病机制”的系统综述发表于欧洲医学研究杂志,总结了现有的人类研究;这是一项学术性综述,而非新的暴发报告(方法和范围证据见N3)。 [news-ee1966357d48737a]
A hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections, and additional suspected cases. [news-1449a883ab9cc937]
新堡大学传染病专家克雷格·达尔顿(Dr Craig Dalton)评论了一艘游轮上出现的汉坦病毒 暴发,表示这种病毒不太可能成为下一个全球大流行病。 [news-cdae10e3ab7598ef]
CDC在皮尼岭近期的健康评估中对样本进行了检测,未发现确认的汉坦病毒感染病例。CDC作为皮尼岭健康评估的一部分进行了检测,结果显示未确认汉坦病毒感染病例。该报告来自KOTA地区新闻。 [news-d8873c87024c9dac]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Hantaviruses news developments.
key_findings_en: PAHO Director emphasized the importance of laboratory preparedness in responding to health threats, using hantavirus as an example of how integrated systems are essential for effective public health action. [news-4558c5b2cb403687]

A systematic review titled “Immunopathogenesis of vascular leakage in hantavirus infections” was published in the European Journal of Medical Research, summarising existing human studies; this is a scholarly synthesis, not a new outbreak report (evidence of methods and scope in N3). [news-ee1966357d48737a]

A hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections, and additional suspected cases. The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported the incident, and the CDC classified it as a Level 3 emergency response. [news-1449a883ab9cc937]

Dr Craig Dalton, a University of Newcastle communicable disease expert, commented on a cruise ship outbreak of hantavirus, stating it is unlikely to become the next global pandemic. [news-cdae10e3ab7598ef]

CDC testing found no confirmed hantavirus infection in specimens from a recent Pine Ridge health evaluation. The CDC conducted testing as part of a health evaluation in Pine Ridge, and the results indicated no confirmed cases of hantavirus infection. The report is from KOTA Territory News. [news-d8873c87024c9dac]

papers.title: Hantavirus preparedness at human-rodent interfaces: lessons from China's HFRS control and Andes virus transmission in mobile populations.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are globally distributed reservoir-associated viruses that cause haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), mainly in Eurasia, and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS; also termed hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, HPS), mainly in the Americas. Most human infections arise from exposure to rodent-contaminated environments, so clustered disease may reflect shared environmental exposure rather than interpersonal transmission. This Review uses China's long-term HFRS experience as a central case study for interface-centred preparedness. China demonstrates that sustained surveillance, reservoir monitoring, risk-defined vaccination, rodent control and environmental risk reduction can substantially reduce disease burden, but declining incidence does not mean disappearance of ecological risk. Its dual HTNV and SEOV ecology further shows that one clinical syndrome can arise from distinct agricultural and peri-domestic rat-associated interfaces. Andes virus (ANDV) provides a contrasting challenge: selected outbreaks have documented limited but consequential human-to-human transmission after close or prolonged contact. The 2026 MV Hondius event illustrates how such transmission can become an international contact-tracing problem when it occurs in mobile populations. Preparedness should therefore combine long-term management of rodent-derived interfaces, rapid discrimination between common-source clusters and ANDV secondary transmission, and response systems that remain effective when exposed persons, infected animals or close contacts cross geographical borders.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on hantaviruses, which are globally distributed reservoir-associated viruses causing hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in the Americas. The review highlights the importance of rodent-contaminated environments as a primary source of human infections, emphasizing that clustered disease often reflects shared environmental exposure rather than interpersonal transmission. China's long-term HFRS experience is used as a central case study to demonstrate how sustained surveillance, reservoir monitoring, risk-defined vaccination, rodent control, and environmental risk reduction can significantly reduce disease burden. However, declining incidence does not equate to the disappearance of ecological risk. The dual ecology of HTNV and SEOV illustrates that one clinical syndrome can arise from distinct agricultural and peri-domestic rat-associated interfaces. In contrast, Andes virus (ANDV) presents a unique challenge due to limited but consequential human-to-human transmission in close or prolonged contact scenarios. The 2026 MV Hondius event exemplifies how ANDV transmission in mobile populations can become an international contact-tracing issue. The review concludes that preparedness must integrate long-term rodent-derived interface management, rapid discrimination between common-source clusters and ANDV secondary transmission, and response systems that remain effective across geographical boundaries.

papers.title: Hantavirus infections: A growing global health concern
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are increasingly regarded as an important emerging risk to global health, with an estimated annual impact on more than 200000 people worldwide. These pathogens are single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Han taviridae and are known to cause two major clinical syndromes in humans: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). The so-called old world hantaviruses, which are associated with HFRS, are predominantly distributed across Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa. In contrast, new world hantaviruses, responsible for HPS, are largely confined to North and South America. Each year, approximately 150000-200000 HFRS cases require hospitalization globally, with the greatest burden occurring in developing regions. The mortality rate of HFRS ranges from below 1% to about 12%, depending on the infecting strain. Both disease forms are characterized by increased capillary permeability, leading to clinical features such as hypotension, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis. While HFRS has a broader geographic distribution, HPS carries a higher risk of death.. Moreover, the detection of new viral strains and the steady rise in reported cases have intensified global concern. Enhancing surveillance systems and expanding laboratory diagnostic capacity are therefore essential for effective monitoring and control of hantavirus diseases.

These pathogens are single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Han taviridae and are known to cause two major clinical syndromes in humans: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). The so-called old world hantaviruses, which are associated with HFRS, are predominantly distributed across Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa. In contrast, new world hantaviruses, responsible for HPS, are largely confined to North and South America. Each year, approximately 150000-200000 HFRS cases require hospitalization globally, with the greatest burden occurring in developing regions. The mortality rate of HFRS ranges from below 1% to about 12%, depending on the infecting strain. Both disease forms are characterized by increased capillary permeability, leading to clinical features such as hypotension, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis. While HFRS has a broader geographic distribution, HPS carries a higher risk of death.. Moreover, the detection of new viral strains and the steady rise in reported cases have intensified global concern. Enhancing surveillance systems and expanding laboratory diagnostic capacity are therefore essential for effective monitoring and control of hantavirus diseases.

Old world hantaviruses, linked to HFRS, are primarily found in Asia, Europe, and parts of Africa, while new world hantaviruses, responsible for HPS, are mainly in North and South America. The review emphasizes the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic systems to manage hantavirus diseases effectively. However, it notes gaps in understanding the geographic distribution of HPS, the mechanisms of capillary permeability, and specific interventions for these infections.

papers.title: Immunopathogenesis of vascular leakage in hantavirus infections: a systematic review of mechanisms underlying HPS and HFRS
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infections manifest as Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) and Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), both associated with increased vascular permeability despite the lack of direct cytopathic injury to endothelial cells. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2020–May 2026) identified human studies investigating immunopathogenic mechanisms in HPS or HFRS. Due to substantial heterogeneity across study designs, findings were synthesized descriptively. Forty-one studies (39 cohorts, 2 case–control) were included, predominantly on HFRS-associated hantaviruses (HTNV, PUUV, DOBV); only one study evaluated HPS-associated ANDV. The reviewed literature revealed elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-18, CXCL10, CX3CL1), depletion of Mucosal-Associated Invariant T (MAIT) cells linked to IRE1αdependent pyroptosis, disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx, and coagulation disturbances with platelet dysfunction. Biomarkers of glycocalyx injury (heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and soluble thrombomodulin) were associated with increased mortality risk (AUC 0.87–0.93). No human mechanistic studies on Sin Nombre virus (SNV) were identified. Hantavirus-induced vascular leakage is driven by cytokine-mediated endothelial dysfunction, MAIT cell pyroptosis, glycocalyx degradation, and immunothrombosis. While HFRS mechanisms are now well-characterized, the absence of human mechanistic data for HPS—particularly for SNV—remains a critical gap.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the immunopathogenesis of vascular leakage in hantavirus infections, focusing on Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) and Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS). The review identifies 41 studies, primarily on HFRS-associated hantaviruses such as Hantaan virus (HTNV), Puumala virus (PUUV), and Dobrava-Belgrade virus (DOBV), with only one study examining HPS-associated Andes virus (ANDV). The evidence highlights elevated inflammatory cytokines, MAIT cell pyroptosis, endothelial glycocalyx disruption, and coagulation disturbances as key mechanisms. Biomarkers of glycocalyx injury are linked to increased mortality risk. Despite substantial heterogeneity, the findings are synthesized descriptively. The review notes a critical gap in human mechanistic studies on Sin Nombre virus (SNV), which is associated with HPS. The review underscores the need for further research on SNV and other hantaviruses to better understand vascular leakage mechanisms and improve clinical management.

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述的文献显示,炎症细胞因子(IL-6、IL-18、CXCL10、CX3CL1)升高,与IRE1α依赖性焦亡相关的黏膜相关不变T(MAIT)细胞减少,内皮细胞糖萼的破坏,以及凝血功能障碍与血小板功能障碍。糖萼损伤的生物标志物(肝素硫酸盐、硫酸软骨素和可溶性血栓调节蛋白)与增加的死亡率风险相关(AUC 0.87–0.93)。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于研究设计存在显著异质性,结果以描述性方式综合。未发现关于Sin Nombre病毒(SNV)的人类机制研究。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 汉坦病毒诱导的血管渗漏由细胞因子介导的内皮功能障碍、MAIT细胞焦亡、糖萼降解和免疫凝血驱动。尽管HFRS的机制已较为明确,但HPS(尤其是SNV)缺乏人类机制数据仍然是一个关键的空白。

papers.title: Differences in Ecological Drivers for Leptospira and Hantavirus in an Urban Norway Rat Population.
papers.abstract: Abstract Rodent control in urban areas is an important public health measure, among other reasons, for their capacity of harboring several zoonotic pathogens. Efficient, evidence-based control programs must consider both rodent and pathogen ecology, to achieve both rodent population and pathogen transmission risk reduction. The present study aims to determine the ecological drivers of Leptospira and Hantavirus positivity in an urban Norway Rat population. One hundred and twenty rats were trapped in four urban poor communities in Salvador, Brazil, tested for Leptospira sp. Generalized Linear Models for Leptospira (N=109) and Hantavirus (N=108) positivity were created with a pool of environmental and demographic variables, followed by stepwise model selection using Akaike’s Information Criterion. Age, presence of Calodium hepaticum scars, wounds, accumulated materials, open sewer canals and unpaved soil were positively associated with Leptospira positivity. Age and presence of accumulated materials were positively associated with Hantavirus positivity, while rodent control campaigns and being male were protective factors. Factors associated with positivity for Leptospira are also associated with rodent infestation. Different subsets of environmental and demographic factors influence pathogens with different epidemiological characteristics. Control measures that effectively reduce zoonotic risk must consider the ecological characteristics of the pathogens present in the system.
authors: Ana Maria Borges da Paixão Barreto

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the ecological drivers of Leptospira and Hantavirus in urban Norway Rat populations, as these rodents are known to harbor zoonotic pathogens. The research aimed to identify factors influencing the presence of these pathogens in the environment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in four urban poor communities in Salvador, Brazil, where 120 Norway Rats were trapped and tested for Leptospira and Hantavirus. The study focused on environmental and demographic variables associated with the rats.
analysis.methods: Generalized Linear Models were used to analyze Leptospira (N=109) and Hantavirus (N=108) positivity, incorporating a pool of environmental and demographic variables. Stepwise model selection was performed using Akaike’s Information Criterion.
analysis.main_results: Age, presence of Calodium hepaticum scars, wounds, accumulated materials, open sewer canals, and unpaved soil were positively associated with Leptospira positivity. Age and presence of accumulated materials were positively associated with Hantavirus positivity, while rodent control campaigns and being male were protective factors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that different subsets of environmental and demographic factors influence the epidemiological characteristics of the pathogens. This finding highlights the need for tailored control strategies based on pathogen-specific ecological drivers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted rodent control programs that consider the ecological characteristics of specific pathogens, thereby reducing zoonotic transmission risks in urban settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on associations rather than experimental data, and the generalizability of findings may be constrained by the specific urban environment studied.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the ecological drivers of Leptospira and Hantavirus in an urban Norway Rat population in Salvador, Brazil. It highlights that factors such as age, wounds, accumulated materials, and environmental conditions are associated with pathogen positivity. The research underscores the importance of considering pathogen-specific ecological characteristics in designing effective rodent control programs. While the study provides valuable insights, its cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the findings may not be broadly generalizable. The results suggest that tailored interventions are necessary to mitigate zoonotic risks in urban areas.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the ecological drivers of Leptospira and Hantavirus in urban Norway Rat populations, as these rodents are known to harbor zoonotic pathogens. The research aimed to identify factors influencing the presence of these pathogens in the environment.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in four urban poor communities in Salvador, Brazil, where 120 Norway Rats were trapped and tested for Leptospira and Hantavirus. The study focused on environmental and demographic variables associated with the rats.
elements_en.methods: Generalized Linear Models were used to analyze Leptospira (N=109) and Hantavirus (N=108) positivity, incorporating a pool of environmental and demographic variables. Stepwise model selection was performed using Akaike’s Information Criterion.
elements_en.main_results: Age, presence of Calodium hepaticum scars, wounds, accumulated materials, open sewer canals, and unpaved soil were positively associated with Leptospira positivity. Age and presence of accumulated materials were positively associated with Hantavirus positivity, while rodent control campaigns and being male were protective factors.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that different subsets of environmental and demographic factors influence the epidemiological characteristics of the pathogens. This finding highlights the need for tailored control strategies based on pathogen-specific ecological drivers.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted rodent control programs that consider the ecological characteristics of specific pathogens, thereby reducing zoonotic transmission risks in urban settings.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on associations rather than experimental data, and the generalizability of findings may be constrained by the specific urban environment studied.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解城市挪威鼠种群中莱普托斯珀里拉和汉坦病毒的生态驱动因素,因为这些鼠类已知能够携带人兽共患病原体。研究旨在确定这些病原体在环境中的存在影响因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在巴西萨尔瓦多市的四个城市贫困社区中进行,捕捉并检测了120只挪威鼠,以了解与鼠类相关的环境和人口学变量。
elements_zh.methods: 使用广义线性模型分析莱普托斯珀里拉(N=109)和汉坦病毒(N=108)的阳性率,纳入了环境和人口学变量池。采用Akaike信息准则进行逐步模型选择。
elements_zh.main_results: 年龄、Calodium hepaticum疤痕、伤口、堆积物、开放排污沟渠和未铺装土壤与莱普托斯珀里拉阳性率呈正相关。年龄和堆积物的存在与汉坦病毒阳性率呈正相关,而鼠类控制活动和雄性特征则具有保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,不同的环境和人口学因素子集影响病原体的流行病学特征。这一发现强调了根据病原体特定的生态驱动因素制定针对性控制策略的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发考虑特定病原体生态学特征的针对性鼠类控制计划提供信息,从而在城市环境中降低人兽共患病传播的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法确定因果关系。证据强度中等,因为它是基于相关性而非实验数据,且研究结果的可推广性可能受到所研究特定城市环境的限制。

papers.title_zh: 城市挪威鼠种群中莱普托斯珀里拉和汉坦病毒的生态驱动因素差异
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Rodent control in urban areas is an important public health measure, among other reasons, for their capacity of harboring several zoonotic pathogens. Efficient, evidence-based control programs must consider both rodent and pathogen ecology, to achieve both rodent population and pathogen transmission risk reduction. The present study aims to determine the ecological drivers of Leptospira and Hantavirus positivity in an urban Norway Rat population. One hundred and twenty rats were trapped in four urban poor communities in Salvador, Brazil, tested for Leptospira sp. Generalized Linear Models for Leptospira (N=109) and Hantavirus (N=108) positivity were created with a pool of environmental and demographic variables, followed by stepwise model selection using Akaike’s Information Criterion. Age, presence of Calodium hepaticum scars, wounds, accumulated materials, open sewer canals and unpaved soil were positively associated with Leptospira positivity. Age and presence of accumulated materials were positively associated with Hantavirus positivity, while rodent control campaigns and being male were protective factors. Factors associated with positivity for Leptospira are also associated with rodent infestation. Different subsets of environmental and demographic factors influence pathogens with different epidemiological characteristics. Control measures that effectively reduce zoonotic risk must consider the ecological characteristics of the pathogens present in the system.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 城市地区的鼠类控制是重要的公共卫生措施,因为这些鼠类能够携带多种人兽共患病原体。有效的、基于证据的控制计划必须同时考虑鼠类和病原体的生态学,以实现鼠类种群和病原体传播风险的双重降低。本研究旨在确定城市挪威鼠种群中莱普托斯珀里拉和汉坦病毒阳性率的生态驱动因素。在巴西萨尔瓦多市的四个城市贫困社区中捕捉了120只鼠类,并对其进行了莱普托斯珀里拉属的检测。使用Akaike信息准则对环境和人口学变量池进行逐步模型选择,建立了莱普托斯珀里拉(N=109)和汉坦病毒(N=108)阳性的广义线性模型。年龄、Calodium hepaticum疤痕、伤口、堆积物、开放排污沟渠和未铺装土壤与莱普托斯珀里拉阳性率呈正相关。年龄和堆积物的存在与汉坦病毒阳性率呈正相关,而鼠类控制活动和雄性特征则具有保护作用。与莱普托斯珀里拉阳性率相关的因素也与鼠类滋生有关。不同的环境和人口学因素子集影响具有不同流行病学特征的病原体。有效降低人兽共患病风险的控制措施必须考虑系统中存在病原体的生态学特征。

papers.title: Revisiting Animal Reservoirs of Hantavirus and Other Zoonotic Viruses Associated with Cruise Travel: Impact and Prevention
papers.abstract: The sustained growth of international maritime tourism and the expansion of the cruise industry have increased the importance of emerging zoonotic diseases as a significant challenge to global public health. Cruise ships constitute complex epidemiological settings characterized by high population density, rapid international mobility, and constant interaction between humans, animals, and coastal environments, factors that favor the introduction and spread of emerging infectious agents. Potential zoonotic concerns include orthohantaviruses and other zoonotic viruses, such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and avian influenza, which are associated with animal reservoirs and vectors in ports, tourist destinations, and tropical ecosystems. This review examines the ecology of animal reservoirs of orthohantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens relevant to maritime tourism, including peri-urban rodents, bats, migratory birds, and other mammals. It discusses how climate change, coastal urbanization, and environmental change affect viral transmission dynamics. It highlights epidemiological risks linked to international cruises, particularly exposure during ecotourism excursions, pathogen introduction, and challenges for maritime surveillance. The review also addresses travel medicine, biosecurity, and infection control, emphasizing a One Health approach. Strengthening integrated surveillance and prevention systems is essential to ensure safer, more sustainable, and resilient maritime tourism in the 21st century.

papers.abstract_zh: 国际海上旅游业的持续增长和邮轮产业的扩张增加了新兴人兽共患病作为全球公共卫生重大挑战的重要性。邮轮船构成复杂的流行病学环境,其特点是高人口密度、快速的国际流动性以及人类、动物和沿海环境之间的持续互动,这些因素有利于新兴传染病的引入和传播。潜在的人兽共患病关注点包括正汉坦病毒和其它与动物储存宿主及媒介相关的病毒,如登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒、黄热病和禽流感,这些病毒与港口、旅游目的地和热带生态系统中的动物有关。本综述探讨了与海上旅游业相关的动物储存宿主的正汉坦病毒及其他人兽共患病病原体的生态学,包括郊区啮齿动物、蝙蝠、候鸟及其他哺乳动物。它讨论了气候变化、沿海城市化和环境变化如何影响病毒传播动态。它强调了与国际邮轮相关的流行病学风险,特别是生态旅游活动期间的暴露、病原体引入以及对海上监测的挑战。综述还涉及旅行医学、生物安全和感染控制,强调采用“一个健康”方法的重要性。加强整合的监测和预防系统对于确保21世纪更安全、更可持续和更具韧性的海上旅游业至关重要。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 本综述强调了与国际邮轮相关的流行病学风险,特别是生态旅游活动期间的暴露、病原体引入以及对海上监测的挑战。它强调了采用“一个健康”方法以应对旅行医学、生物安全和感染控制的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 本综述指出了在邮轮环境中正汉坦病毒特定传播动态方面的理解不足,以及环境变化对其传播的影响。它还指出缺乏针对邮轮船独特流行病学特征的全面监测系统。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强整合的监测和预防系统对于确保21世纪更安全、更可持续和更具韧性的海上旅游业至关重要。这包括改进生物安全措施、增强感染控制协议,并推广“一个健康”方法以应对人类、动物和环境健康之间的复杂互动。

papers.title: Clinical severity and health-seeking behaviors of cases with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome: A comparative study across spatial clusters in Jiangxi Province, China.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a significant public health concern in Jiangxi Province, China, where both Hantaan (HTNV) and Seoul (SEOV) co-circulate. Previous studies have identified three distinct clusters of HFRS epidemic in Jiangxi Province, characterized by geographical separation and heterogeneous incidence levels. We hypothesized that clinical severity and healthcare-seeking behaviors may vary across these clusters, and thus conducted a retrospective study to examine this hypothesis. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 4,614 HFRS cases (13-year period) from 63 counties. Cases were classified into four areas based on prior spatial study, representing distinct hilly and plain regions with different proximity to major water bodies and mountains. Data on HFRS cases were collected by county-level CDC staff using a nationally standardized case investigation questionnaire. Clinical severity and healthcare-seeking behaviors (hospital level, onset-to-visit interval) were compared. RESULTS: HFRS cases in Cluster I exhibited the highest clinical severity (22.41% severe, 6.65% critical), while cases in Cluster II were strikingly mild (2.62% severe, 1.31% critical). Median onset-to-visit interval was longest in Cluster II (5 days) vs others (2-4 days). Hospital preference varied: Cluster I primarily used Class II hospitals (65.88%); Cluster II showed near-equal use of Class II (48.44%) and III (47.01%); Cluster III and non-clustered areas favored higher-level hospitals. CONCLUSION: Our findings confirmed that Jiangxi Province, though a mixed epidemic focus, exhibited distinct spatial heterogeneity in clinical severity, and healthcare-seeking behaviors. These findings underscore the need for regionally tailored strategies in HFRS prevention and control.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热,HFRS)是中国江西省的重要公共卫生问题,该地区同时流行汉坦病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)。

papers.title_zh: 肾综合征出血热病例的临床严重程度和就医行为:中国江西省不同空间聚集区的比较研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a significant public health concern in Jiangxi Province, China, where both Hantaan (HTNV) and Seoul (SEOV) co-circulate. Previous studies have identified three distinct clusters of HFRS epidemic in Jiangxi Province, characterized by geographical separation and heterogeneous incidence levels. We hypothesized that clinical severity and healthcare-seeking behaviors may vary across these clusters, and thus conducted a retrospective study to examine this hypothesis. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 4,614 HFRS cases (13-year period) from 63 counties. Cases were classified into four areas based on prior spatial study, representing distinct hilly and plain regions with different proximity to major water bodies and mountains. Data on HFRS cases were collected by county-level CDC staff using a nationally standardized case investigation questionnaire. Clinical severity and healthcare-seeking behaviors (hospital level, onset-to-visit interval) were compared. RESULTS: HFRS cases in Cluster I exhibited the highest clinical severity (22.41% severe, 6.65% critical), while cases in Cluster II were strikingly mild (2.62% severe, 1.31% critical). Median onset-to-visit interval was longest in Cluster II (5 days) vs others (2-4 days). Hospital preference varied: Cluster I primarily used Class II hospitals (65.88%); Cluster II showed near-equal use of Class II (48.44%) and III (47.01%); Cluster III and non-clustered areas favored higher-level hospitals. CONCLUSION: Our findings confirmed that Jiangxi Province, though a mixed epidemic focus, exhibited distinct spatial heterogeneity in clinical severity, and healthcare-seeking behaviors. These findings underscore the need for regionally tailored strategies in HFRS prevention and control.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热,HFRS)是中国江西省的重要公共卫生问题,该地区同时流行汉坦病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)。先前研究已识别出江西省的三个不同HFRS流行聚集区,这些聚集区在地理分布上相互分离,且肾综合征出血热水平存在异质性。我们假设这些聚集区的临床严重程度和就医行为可能存在差异,因此进行了一项回顾性研究以检验这一假设。方法:我们回顾性分析了江西省63个县在13年期间报告的4,614例HFRS病例。根据先前的空间研究,病例被分为四个区域,代表不同的山地和平原地区,且与主要水域和山脉的距离不同。病例数据由县级疾病预防控制中心(CDC)工作人员通过全国统一的病例调查问卷收集。比较了临床严重程度和就医行为(医院等级、发病至就诊间隔)。结果:Cluster I中的HFRS病例表现出最高的临床严重程度(22.41%严重,6.65%危重),而Cluster II中的病例则明显较轻(2.62%严重,1.31%危重)。发病至就诊间隔的中位数在Cluster II中最长(5天),而其他区域为2-4天。医院选择偏好存在差异:Cluster I主要使用二级医院(65.88%);Cluster II则二级和三级医院使用比例接近(48.44%和47.01%);Cluster III和非聚集区更倾向于使用更高层级的医院。结论:我们的研究结果证实,尽管江西省是一个混合流行区,但其在临床严重程度和就医行为方面表现出显著的空间异质性。这些发现强调了在HFRS预防和控制中制定区域性策略的必要性。

papers.title: The efficacy of Cordyceps sinensis preparations in improving kidney outcomes among patients with AKI during hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome: evidence from a Chinese cohort.
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is frequently complicated by acute kidney injury (AKI). Although most patients recover from AKI with supportive care, some progress to chronic kidney disease (CKD). The incidence and determinants of CKD progression in patients with HFRS-AKI remain uncertain. Here, 99 patients with HFRS-AKI treated at Jinling Hospital were analyzed retrospectively to determine the rate of CKD progression and identify associated risk factors. Patients were divided into complete recovery (CR) and incomplete recovery (ICR) groups according to CKD progression. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were collected and analyzed. Overall, 27.3% of patients with HFRS-AKI progressed to CKD despite receiving supportive care. Facial flushing was more frequent in the ICR group than in the CR group (40.7% vs. Multivariate analysis revealed that treatment with Cordyceps sinensis preparations during the AKI phase was an independent protective factor against incomplete kidney recovery (OR: 0.323, 95% CI: 0.114-0.916, p = 0.034). Inverse probability weighting analysis further demonstrated that the use of Cordyceps sinensis preparations was inversely associated with incomplete kidney recovery (β: -1.184, 95% CI: -2.224 - -0.144, p = 0.026). Survival analysis confirmed that Cordyceps sinensis preparation therapy was associated with improved kidney outcomes (log-rank test, p = 0.004). This study provides the first clinical evidence that adjunctive therapy with Cordyceps sinensis preparations during HFRS-AKI is associated with improved kidney outcomes, suggesting that Cordyceps sinensis preparations represents a promising therapeutic approach for viral-induced AKI.

papers.title: A clinical cases of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in the context of HIV-infection
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome and Human Immunodeficiency Virus co-infection is a rare occurrence that warrants significant clinical and scientific attention. A comprehensive understanding of the immune-mediated mechanisms underlying the interaction between Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome and HIV is essential for accurate prognostic modeling. This is particularly crucial because co-infection with these two pathogens often correlates with a severe clinical course, increased mortality rate, and significantly prolonged recovery period. This article presents two clinical case reports. The first involves a patient with virally suppressed HIV infection. The patient experienced a severe clinical course of Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome despite strict adherence to antiretroviral therapy. After receiving intensive treatment, the patient showed clinical improvement and was discharged in stable condition. The second case highlights the progression of Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome in a patient with profound immunosuppression. This one was characterized by a series of complications that resulted in a fatal outcome. The fundamental interaction between these two pathogens is not yet fully understood. This highlights the critical necessity for continued investigation.

papers.title_original: Spatiotemporal correlation analysis between climate change and hantavirus outbreak in Argentina: Quantitative causal inference based on Google Earth Engine and Bayesian spatiotemporal

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the spatiotemporal correlation between climate change and hantavirus outbreaks in Argentina. The background highlights the need to understand how environmental factors may influence the emergence and spread of hantaviruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Argentina, focusing on hantavirus outbreaks and their relationship with climate change. The research spanned multiple years, analyzing data from various geographical regions to capture spatiotemporal patterns.
analysis.methods: The study employed quantitative causal inference methods using Google Earth Engine and Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling to analyze the correlation between climate change and hantavirus outbreaks. These methods were used to process and interpret environmental and epidemiological data.
analysis.main_results: The study found a significant spatiotemporal correlation between climate change indicators and hantavirus outbreak patterns in Argentina. Specific results included the identification of key environmental factors associated with outbreak occurrences.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the results as evidence of a causal relationship between climate change and hantavirus outbreaks, suggesting that environmental changes may influence the virus's transmission dynamics. This approach is novel in its integration of remote sensing and Bayesian modeling for such analyses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for predicting and preventing hantavirus outbreaks by linking them to climate change patterns. This could enhance surveillance and preparedness in affected regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by potential biases in data collection and the complexity of attributing outbreaks solely to climate change. However, the use of advanced modeling techniques provides a moderate level of confidence in the causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the spatiotemporal correlation between climate change and hantavirus outbreaks in Argentina using Google Earth Engine and Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling. The research highlights the need to understand how environmental factors may influence the spread of hantaviruses, which are associated with human disease. The authors found a significant correlation between climate change indicators and outbreak patterns, suggesting that environmental changes may impact transmission dynamics. This approach is novel in its integration of remote sensing and Bayesian modeling. The findings can inform public health strategies for outbreak prediction and prevention. However, the study's evidence is limited by potential biases and the complexity of attributing outbreaks solely to climate change, resulting in a moderate level of confidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发在阿根廷的时空相关性。背景强调了理解环境因素如何影响汉坦病毒出现和传播的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在阿根廷进行,关注汉坦病毒 暴发及其与气候变迁的关系。研究覆盖了多个年份,分析了不同地理区域的数据以捕捉时空模式。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用基于Google Earth Engine和贝叶斯时空建模的定量因果推断方法,分析气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发之间的相关性。这些方法用于处理和解释环境与流行病学数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究发现气候变迁指标与阿根廷汉坦病毒 暴发模式之间存在显著的时空相关性。具体结果包括识别与暴发发生相关的关键环境因素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将结果解释为气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发之间存在因果关系的证据,表明环境变化可能影响该病毒的传播动态。这种方法在整合遥感技术和贝叶斯建模进行此类分析方面具有创新性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为通过与气候变迁模式关联来预测和预防汉坦病毒 暴发的公共卫生策略提供信息。这可能增强受影响地区的监测和应对能力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据受到数据收集潜在偏差和将暴发完全归因于气候变迁的复杂性限制。然而,使用先进的建模技术为因果推断提供了中等程度的置信度。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发在阿根廷的时空相关性。背景强调了理解环境因素如何影响汉坦病毒出现和传播的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在阿根廷进行,关注汉坦病毒 暴发及其与气候变迁的关系。研究覆盖了多个年份,分析了不同地理区域的数据以捕捉时空模式。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用基于Google Earth Engine和贝叶斯时空建模的定量因果推断方法,分析气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发之间的相关性。这些方法用于处理和解释环境与流行病学数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 本研究发现气候变迁指标与阿根廷汉坦病毒 暴发模式之间存在显著的时空相关性。具体结果包括识别与暴发发生相关的关键环境因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将结果解释为气候变迁与汉坦病毒 暴发之间存在因果关系的证据,表明环境变化可能影响该病毒的传播动态。这种方法在整合遥感技术和贝叶斯建模进行此类分析方面具有创新性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为通过与气候变迁模式关联来预测和预防汉坦病毒 暴发的公共卫生策略提供信息。这可能增强受影响地区的监测和应对能力。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据受到数据收集潜在偏差和将暴发完全归因于气候变迁的复杂性限制。然而,使用先进的建模技术为因果推断提供了中等程度的置信度。

papers.title: Emerging evidence of sand fly fever virus transmission in Sri Lanka.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sand fly fever virus (SFFV) infection is an acute self-limiting febrile illness caused by phleboviruses and transmitted by sand flies of the Phlebotomus species. The disease has been reported in the Mediterranean region, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, and is now considered to be expanding into new geographic areas. Clinically, SFFV infection closely resembles acute dengue fever. AIM: To detect other possible infection including SSFV in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever with negative serology results for NS1 antigen. METHODS: In this study, a total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients clinically suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three major hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Patients were from the Colombo and Kandy District, and demographic information was obtained from laboratory request forms, although detailed individual-level demographic data were limited due to anonymization in this laboratory-based study. All samples were initially screened for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further tested for a panel of pathogens including SFFV immunoglobulin (Ig) M, hantavirus IgM, chikungunya IgM, and leptospira IgM antibodies, as well as molecular detection of hantavirus, flavivirus, and alphavirus RNA. RESULTS: From tested samples, two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. These two SFFV-positive cases were from Kandy District and included one child (6-8 years) and one adult (40-50 years), both presenting with uncomplicated dengue-like illness. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka. Given the high endemicity of dengue in the country, SFFV infections may be clinically misdiagnosed as dengue and therefore remain under-recognized. Further studies involving febrile patients and sand fly vector surveillance are required to determine the true burden and epidemiological significance of SFFV in Sri Lanka.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to detect other possible infections, including SFFV, in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever who had negative NS1 antigen results. Serum samples were collected from three hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. papers.title_zh: 斯里兰卡出现沙蝇热病毒传播的新兴证据。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Sand fly fever virus (SFFV) infection is an acute self-limiting febrile illness caused by phleboviruses and transmitted by sand flies of the Phlebotomus species. The disease has been reported in the Mediterranean region, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, and is now considered to be expanding into new geographic areas. Clinically, SFFV infection closely resembles acute dengue fever. AIM: To detect other possible infection including SSFV in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever with negative serology results for NS1 antigen. METHODS: In this study, a total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients clinically suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three major hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Patients were from the Colombo and Kandy District, and demographic information was obtained from laboratory request forms, although detailed individual-level demographic data were limited due to anonymization in this laboratory-based study. All samples were initially screened for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further tested for a panel of pathogens including SFFV immunoglobulin (Ig) M, hantavirus IgM, chikungunya IgM, and leptospira IgM antibodies, as well as molecular detection of hantavirus, flavivirus, and alphavirus RNA. RESULTS: From tested samples, two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. These two SFFV-positive cases were from Kandy District and included one child (6-8 years) and one adult (40-50 years), both presenting with uncomplicated dengue-like illness. CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka. Given the high endemicity of dengue in the country, SFFV infections may be clinically misdiagnosed as dengue and therefore remain under-recognized. Further studies involving febrile patients and sand fly vector surveillance are required to determine the true burden and epidemiological significance of SFFV in Sri Lanka.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:沙蝇热病毒(SFFV)感染是由沙蝇属(Phlebotomus)传播的一种急性自限性发热性疾病。该疾病已在地中海地区、北非、中东和南亚次大陆被报道,目前被认为正在向新的地理区域扩展。临床表现上,SFFV感染与急性登革热极为相似。目的:检测临床疑似登革热但NS1抗原检测为阴性的患者中是否存在其他可能的感染,包括SFFV。方法:本研究从斯里兰卡三家主要医院收集了757份血清样本,这些样本来自2023年1月至8月期间因临床疑似登革热而入院的患者。患者来自科伦坡和坎迪区,尽管通过实验室申请表获得了人口统计信息,但由于本研究为基于实验室的分析,详细个体层面的人口统计数据有限。所有样本首先检测登革热NS1抗原阴性,随后进一步检测包括SFFV免疫球蛋白(Ig)M、汉坦病毒 IgM、基孔肯雅病毒IgM和钩端螺旋体IgM抗体的病原体面板,以及汉坦病毒、黄病毒和甲病毒的RNA分子检测。结果:在检测的样本中,有2份样本通过商业免疫印迹检测显示对SFFV特异性IgM呈阳性,而所有其他检测登革热、基孔肯雅病毒、钩端螺旋体、汉坦病毒及相关RNA病毒的结果均为阴性。这2例SFFV阳性病例来自坎迪区,包括一名儿童(6-8岁)和一名成人(40-50岁),两者均表现为非复杂性登革热样疾病。结论:本研究首次提供了斯里兰卡SFFV感染的证据。鉴于该国登革热的高流行性,SFFV感染可能被误诊为登革热,从而未被充分认识。需要进一步研究发热患者和沙蝇媒介 监测,以确定SFFV在斯里兰卡的真实负担和流行病学意义。

papers.title: Seasonal Dynamics, Host Network Structure, and Environmental Drivers of Gamasid Mite Communities on Small Mammals in a Dry–Hot Valley: A Year-Round Monitoring Study
papers.abstract: Ectoparasitic gamasid mites on small mammals play crucial roles in transmitting zoonotic pathogens like hantaviruses associated with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). To elucidate their community, network structure, and seasonal drivers in xeric habitats, a consecutive 12-month localized survey was conducted in Waxi Village, Binchuan County, a dry–hot valley in Yunnan Province, southwest China, from November 2020 to October 2021. From 1329 captured small mammals (18 species, 89.62% rodents), 12,075 gamasid mites belonging to 33 species were identified. The community exhibited overwhelming dominance by the family Laelapidae (Cr = 99.35%) and genus Laelaps (Cr = 97.37%). Laelaps algericus, L. guizhouensis, and L. nuttalli constituted the dominant mite species (cumulative Cr = 88.96%) and formed a tightly correlated core species cluster. Overall infestation prevalence (PM), mean intensity (MI), and mean abundance (MA) were 46.05%, 19.73 mites/host, and 9.09 mites/host, respectively. The bipartite host–gamasid network revealed a significantly nested architecture (NODFobs = 31.16, Z = 14.03, p < 0.001) with high specialization (H2′ = 0.599), anchored by dominant hosts (Rattus andamanensis, Apodemus chevrieri, and Mus caroli). α-diversity analysis showed that Margalef richness, Shannon–Wiener index, and Gini–Simpson index peaked in autumn (November), while troughs occurred in mid-spring (April) and mid-autumn (October). Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS, stress = 0.0048) and PERMANOVA (R2 = 0.074, p = 0.001) confirmed significant seasonal shifts in community composition. Standard redundancy analysis (RDA) suggested temperature as the primary climatic driver (F = 7.205, p = 0.001; total model explanation = 8.2%). However, partial RDA (pRDA) conditioning on host species identity demonstrated that climatic variables directly accounted for only 0.1% of net variance (F = 0.662, p = 0.521). Our findings indicate that gamasid mite community assembly in this dry–hot valley is characterized by strong species dominance and network nestedness and that seasonal fluctuations are consistent with a host-mediated pattern rather than being directly governed by climate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the seasonal dynamics, host network structure, and environmental drivers of gamasid mite communities on small mammals in a dry–hot valley in Yunnan Province, China. The research highlights the dominance of the Laelapidae family and the genus Laelaps, with three species forming a core cluster. The study found that the mite community exhibited a nested network structure and high specialization, with dominant hosts playing a key role. Seasonal fluctuations were observed, and while temperature was identified as a primary climatic driver, the analysis suggested that host-mediated patterns may be more influential. papers.abstract_zh: 小型哺乳动物体表寄生的Gamasid螨类在传播如汉坦病毒等与肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热)相关的动物源性病原体中起着关键作用。为阐明其群落结构、网络特征及季节性驱动因素,本研究在云南省西南部干热谷地区宾川县瓦西村进行了连续12个月的本地化调查,调查时间为2020年11月至2021年10月。从捕获的1329只小型哺乳动物(18种,其中89.62%为啮齿类动物)中,鉴定出12,075只属于33种的Gamasid螨类。该群落以Laelapidae科(Cr = 99.35%)和Laelaps属(Cr = 97.37%)为主导。Laelaps algericus、L. guizhouensis和L. nuttalli构成了主要螨类物种(累积Cr = 88.96%),并形成了紧密相关的核心物种群。总体感染率(PM)、平均感染强度(MI)和平均丰度(MA)分别为46.05%、19.73只/宿主和9.09只/宿主。双模态宿主–Gamasid网络显示其具有显著的嵌套结构(NODFobs = 31.16,Z = 14.03,p < 0.001),并表现出高度的专业化(H2′ = 0.599),主要由优势宿主(Rattus andamanensis、Apodemus chevrieri和Mus caroli)锚定。α多样性分析显示,Margalef丰富度、Shannon–Wiener指数和Gini–Simpson指数在秋季(11月)达到峰值,而在春末(4月)和秋末(10月)出现低谷。非度量多维尺度分析(NMDS,stress = 0.0048)和PERMANOVA(R2 = 0.074,p = 0.001)证实了群落组成的显著季节性变化。标准冗余分析(RDA)表明温度是主要的气候驱动因素(F = 7.205,p = 0.001;总模型解释度 = 8.2%)。然而,通过以宿主物种身份为条件的偏冗余分析(pRDA),发现气候变量仅直接解释了净变异性的0.1%(F = 0.662,p = 0.521)。我们的研究结果表明,该干热谷中Gamasid螨类群落的组装特征主要表现为物种主导和网络嵌套性,其季节性波动更符合由宿主介导的模式,而非直接由气候因素驱动。

Search Search Home News UNGA81: Robust laboratory systems key to preventing, detecting and responding to health threats UNGA81: Robust laboratory systems key to preventing, detecting and responding to health threats At a side event co-organized by the Mérieux Foundation USA, Weill Cornell Medicine, GHESKIO Centers and PAHO, PAHO Director highlights lessons from the Americas and the importance of sustained investment in laboratory capacity between crises New York, September 21, 2026 (PAHO) – Robust laboratory systems are essential to prevent, detect and respond to health threats, and require sustained investment between crises, Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa said today at a high-level event on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Dr. Jarbas Barbosa speaking at the event titled: “Crisis in preparedness: laboratories and frontline readiness in the time of Ebola.” Speaking at the event, “Crisis in preparedness: laboratories and frontline readiness in the time of Ebola,” Dr. Barbosa highlighted lessons from the Americas, emphasizing that laboratory preparedness is much more than sophisticated equipment or the ability of a national reference laboratory to perform a specialized test. It is a system that must enable countries to detect unusual events, safely collect and refer specimens, provide timely and reliable diagnosis, share information across institutions and borders, and rapidly translate laboratory findings into public health action. While Ebola is not currently circulating in the Americas, PAHO has been working with countries to prepare for the possibility of imported cases. Following the Ebola outbreak in Africa earlier this year, PAHO strengthened regional preparedness, supporting countries to reinforce surveillance, laboratory diagnosis, biosafety, infection prevention and control, and the safe referral of samples to specialized laboratories. Dr. Barbosa highlighted recent experience with hantavirus as an example of how laboratory, genomic and epidemiological capacities must work together. In 2025, eight countries in the Region reported more than 200 confirmed cases and 60 deaths. PAHO issued an epidemiological alert, strengthened diagnostic protocols and conducted regional training with reference laboratories and WHO Collaborating Centers in Argentina, the United States and Panama. These capacities were soon put to the test when a cluster of Andes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome associated with the MV Hondius cruise ship became an international public health event. PAHO helped establish communication between the countries involved and ANLIS-Malbrán in Argentina, bringing specialized Andes virus diagnostic expertise into the investigation. As contacts were identified in Spain, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and eventually Canada, laboratories, epidemiologists and public health authorities were able to exchange information and coordinate rapidly. PAHO also collaborated with the genomic team characterizing the virus, connecting laboratory and genomic findings with the epidemiological investigation and risk assessment. Dr. Barbosa emphasized that this integration of diagnostics, genomic surveillance, epidemiology and public health decision-making is essential to effective preparedness. PAHO continues to strengthen regional genomic surveillance through PAHOGen, PAHO’s Genomic Surveillance Regional Networks, connecting capacities and expertise across the Americas. “The hantavirus experience illustrates an important principle: Not every country needs to maintain every highly specialized diagnostic or genomic capacity. But every country must be able to rapidly access those capacities through trusted national, regional and international networks when they are needed,” Dr. Barbosa said. He emphasized that when a public health event crosses borders, there is no time to begin identifying experts, reference laboratories, diagnostic protocols, specimen-referral pathways or channels for communicating results. These relationships and mechanisms must already be in place. Preparedness therefore requires sustained investment in adaptable molecular platforms, trained professionals, quality-management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, reliable specimen referral and transport, resilient supply chains, interoperable information systems, and strong national and regional laboratory networks. “Preparedness is built between emergencies,” Dr. Barbosa said. The surveillance systems, laboratory protocols, genomic expertise, trained professionals and trusted relationships strengthened during routine periods are the same capacities that allow countries to detect unusual events earlier, understand them faster and act before they become larger emergencies. “That is not simply an investment in laboratories. It is an investment in stronger health systems, health security, preparedness and resilience,” he added. The event brought together global and regional leaders to discuss how to strengthen laboratory systems as a cornerstone of pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, drawing on lessons from Ebola, COVID-19, H5N1 influenza and other emerging and reemerging infectious diseases. The event focused on practical solutions for strengthening laboratory systems for both routine health services and pandemic preparedness, including the need for sustained investment in clinical laboratory capacity. Other speakers included Dr. Chikwe Ihekweazu, Executive Director of the WHO Health Emergencies Programme; Dr. Robert Harrington, Stephen and Suzanne Weiss Dean at Weill Cornell Medicine; and Dr. Robert Sebbag, Vice President of the Mérieux Foundation. Search Search Home News UNGA81: Robust laboratory systems key to preventing, detecting and responding to health threats UNGA81: Robust laboratory systems key to preventing, detecting and responding to health threats At a side event co-organized by the Mérieux Foundation USA, Weill Cornell Medicine, GHESKIO Centers and PAHO, PAHO Director highlights lessons from the Americas and the importance of sustained investment in laboratory capacity between crises New York, September 21, 2026 (PAHO) – Robust laboratory systems are essential to prevent, detect and respond to health threats, and require sustained investment between crises, Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa said today at a high-level event on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Dr. Jarbas Barbosa speaking at the event titled: “Crisis in preparedness: laboratories and frontline readiness in the time of Ebola.” Speaking at the event, “Crisis in preparedness: laboratories and frontline readiness in the time of Ebola,” Dr. Barbosa highlighted lessons from the Americas, emphasizing that laboratory preparedness is much more than sophisticated equipment or the ability of a national reference laboratory to perform a specialized test. It is a system that must enable countries to detect unusual events, safely collect and refer specimens, provide timely and reliable diagnosis, share information across institutions and borders, and rapidly translate laboratory findings into public health action. While Ebola is not currently circulating in the Americas, PAHO has been working with countries to prepare for the possibility of imported cases. Following the Ebola outbreak in Africa earlier this year, PAHO strengthened regional preparedness, supporting countries to reinforce surveillance, laboratory diagnosis, biosafety, infection prevention and control, and the safe referral of samples to specialized laboratories. Dr. Barbosa highlighted recent experience with hantavirus as an example of how laboratory, genomic and epidemiological capacities must work together. In 2025, eight countries in the Region reported more than 200 confirmed cases and 60 deaths. PAHO issued an epidemiological alert, strengthened diagnostic protocols and conducted regional training with reference laboratories and WHO Collaborating Centers in Argentina, the United States and Panama. These capacities were soon put to the test when a cluster of Andes hantavirus pulmonary syndrome associated with the MV Hondius cruise ship became an international public health event. PAHO helped establish communication between the countries involved and ANLIS-Malbrán in Argentina, bringing specialized Andes virus diagnostic expertise into the investigation. As contacts were identified in Spain, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and eventually Canada, laboratories, epidemiologists and public health authorities were able to exchange information and coordinate rapidly. PAHO also collaborated with the genomic team characterizing the virus, connecting laboratory and genomic findings with the epidemiological investigation and risk assessment. Dr. Barbosa emphasized that this integration of diagnostics, genomic surveillance, epidemiology and public health decision-making is essential to effective preparedness. PAHO continues to strengthen regional genomic surveillance through PAHOGen, PAHO’s Genomic Surveillance Regional Networks, connecting capacities and expertise across the Americas. “The hantavirus experience illustrates an important principle: Not every country needs to maintain every highly specialized diagnostic or genomic capacity. But every country must be able to rapidly access those capacities through trusted national, regional and international networks when they are needed,” Dr. Barbosa said. He emphasized that when a public health event crosses borders, there is no time to begin identifying experts, reference laboratories, diagnostic protocols, specimen-referral pathways or channels for communicating results. These relationships and mechanisms must already be in place. Preparedness therefore requires sustained investment in adaptable molecular platforms, trained professionals, quality-management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, reliable specimen referral and transport, resilient supply chains, interoperable information systems, and strong national and regional laboratory networks. “Preparedness is built between emergencies,” Dr. Barbosa said. The surveillance systems, laboratory protocols, genomic expertise, trained professionals and trusted relationships strengthened during routine periods are the same capacities that allow countries to detect unusual events earlier, understand them faster and act before they become larger emergencies. “That is not simply an investment in laboratories. It is an investment in stronger health systems, health security, preparedness and resilience,” he added. The event brought together global and regional leaders to discuss how to strengthen laboratory systems as a cornerstone of pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, drawing on lessons from Ebola, COVID-19, H5N1 influenza and other emerging and reemerging infectious diseases. The event focused on practical solutions for strengthening laboratory systems for both routine health services and pandemic preparedness, including the need for sustained investment in clinical laboratory capacity. Other speakers included Dr. Chikwe Ihekweazu, Executive Director of the WHO Health Emergencies Programme; Dr. Robert Harrington, Stephen and Suzanne Weiss Dean at Weill Cornell Medicine; and Dr. Robert Sebbag, Vice President of the Mérieux Foundation. news.title_zh: UNGA81: 强健的实验室系统对于预防、检测和应对健康威胁至关重要 - 美洲卫生组织(PAHO)
news.source_body_en: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) highlighted the critical role of robust laboratory systems in preventing, detecting, and responding to health threats during a high-level event at the 81st United Nations General Assembly. Using hantavirus as an example, PAHO Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa emphasized that laboratory preparedness is not just about advanced equipment but about creating systems that enable countries to detect unusual events, safely collect and refer specimens, provide timely diagnosis, and coordinate across borders. In 2025, eight countries in the Americas reported over 200 confirmed cases and 60 deaths linked to hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, with cases spreading internationally. PAHO supported these efforts by issuing an epidemiological alert, strengthening diagnostic protocols, and conducting regional training with reference laboratories. news.content_zh: 美洲卫生组织(PAHO)在第81届联合国大会高级别活动上强调了强健实验室系统在预防、检测和应对健康威胁中的关键作用。以汉坦病毒为例,PAHO主任博士Jarbas Barbosa指出,实验室准备不仅关乎先进设备,更在于建立能够使各国检测异常事件、安全采集和转送样本、及时提供诊断以及跨境协调的系统。2025年,美洲地区八个国报告了超过200例确认病例和60例与汉坦病毒肺综合征相关的死亡,病例已出现国际传播。PAHO通过发布流行病学警报、加强诊断协议以及与参考实验室开展区域培训,支持了这些努力。暴发通过快速信息交换和基因组特征分析得以管理,这突显了持续投资于适应性强的分子平台、专业人员和可信赖网络的必要性,以确保有效的公共卫生响应。

news.content: 00:00/02:13 10 859.7K Advertisement|Remove ads. A hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship has resulted in three deaths and raised global health concerns. Hundreds of people watch as the cruise ship "Disney Adventure" sets sail in the southwestern Baltic Sea, Germany, on September 01, 2025. (Photo by Jens Büttner/picture alliance via Getty Images) - WHO said affected passengers developed symptoms ranging from fever and stomach issues to severe respiratory complications. - Carnival, Norwegian Cruise Line, and Royal Caribbean declined by up to 1% overnight. - The CDC classified the hantavirus outbreak as a low-level Level 3 emergency response. U.S. cruise stocks, including Carnival (CCL), Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH), and Royal Caribbean (RCL), all slipped overnight, causing investor concern after a sudden health scare linked to a South Atlantic voyage rattled confidence in an already sensitivity-prone travel sector. A luxury cruise voyage has turned into a major health incident after a hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius led to three deaths and growing international concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), a cluster of acute respiratory illness cases was first flagged on May 2, involving passengers on a cruise ship carrying 147 people. The vessel, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, in early April, has been anchored off Cabo Verde as authorities coordinate response efforts. WHO noted that symptoms among affected passengers developed between April 6 and April 28, beginning with fever and gastrointestinal distress before rapidly escalating into pneumonia, respiratory failure, and shock in severe cases. WHO said hantaviruses usually spread through infected rodents or contaminated areas. In rare cases, the Andes strain can spread between people in close-contact settings such as shared cabins. Despite the severity of the onboard outbreak, the WHO continues to assess the overall global risk as low. Although global risk assessments remain low, the psychological impact on investors has been evident. Cruise operators' stocks, such as Carnival, Norwegian Cruise Line, and Royal Caribbean, declined by up to 1% overnight after a 2% to 3% decline in the regular session. For many investors, the situation parallels the COVID-19 pandemic, which upended the entire travel industry. Though the U.S. cruise sector has largely recovered from the operational collapse caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, the industry’s largest operators continue to grapple with the long-term consequences of massive borrowing accumulated during the shutdown years. While Royal Caribbean has emerged as the standout performer with returns exceeding 233% over the past five years, rivals CCL and NCLH continue to battle elevated debt burdens and margin pressure. NCLH, in particular, has plunged nearly 40% over the last five years. To make matters worse, last week the company warned that softer travel demand and geopolitical uncertainty are weighing on bookings in key markets and unveiled additional cost-cutting measures to stabilize profits. However, according to a Reuters report, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has categorized the hantavirus outbreak as a Level 3 emergency response, its lowest emergency alert level. So far this year, NCLH and CCL stocks have plunged nearly 23% and 12%, respectively, while RCL stock has gained 0.7%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Trump holds a press conference announcing U.S. Vice President Mike Pence to lead the effort combating the spread of the coronavirus on February 26, 2020. (Photo by Yasin Ozturk/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images) - Trump said that the administration will release a full report on a Hantavirus on Friday. - The outbreak aboard the Dutch-flagged cruise ship Hondius has resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections and additional suspected cases. - Moderna drew attention due to its hantavirus vaccine partnership with Korea University. Shares of vaccine makers and biodefense companies rallied overnight on Friday after U.S. President Donald Trump addressed a deadly hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship and promised a full update on the situation. Overnight, Emergent BioSolutions (EBS) climbed 3%, while Inovio Pharmaceuticals (INO) and Novavax (NVAX) each gained 2% and Moderna (MRNA) rose 1%. Trump said late Thursday that the administration was closely studying the outbreak from the Dutch-flagged cruise ship Hondius, where three passengers have died and several others became infected. “It’s very much, we hope, under control,” Trump said, adding that a full report will be released on Friday. The outbreak has triggered six confirmed infections and additional suspected cases aboard the vessel, which had 150 passengers onboard during an Atlantic voyage from Argentina toward Europe. Authorities are still investigating how the virus spread on board. Singapore has already isolated two passengers from the ship due to concerns about possible exposure during the trip. The World Health Organization (WHO) also issued an alert on the outbreak, although officials said that the global risk remains low and that hantavirus is less transmissible than COVID-19 or influenza. The virus involved is said to be the Andes strain, one of the few hantavirus variants associated with limited human-to-human transmission. Moderna is viewed as one of the U.S. government’s key vaccine platforms for outbreaks. Since 2023, the company has worked with Korea University’s Vaccine Innovation Center on an mRNA-based hantavirus vaccine candidate, with preclinical studies earlier this year showing protection against hantavirus infection in mice. In 2024, Moderna received a $176 million award backed by the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) in 2024 for the development of mRNA-based pandemic influenza vaccines and outbreak preparedness programs. Moderna’s partnership with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) is also in focus, which previously said mRNA could help shorten vaccine-development timelines to as little as 100 days during outbreaks. Inovio, meanwhile, has the clearest hantavirus link among the stocks rallying overnight. The company previously participated in several hantavirus DNA vaccine studies targeting Hantaan, Puumala and Andes hantavirus strains. One National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases-backed study evaluated an Andes virus DNA vaccine to prevent hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, while another U.S. Army-supported study examined mixed hantavirus DNA vaccines. While none of Inovio’s hantavirus vaccine programs produced a commercial product, the outbreak revived speculative interest in companies with prior hantavirus research. Investors frequently rotate into Novavax during virus headlines due to the company’s vaccine-development platform and history of rapidly developing candidates for pathogens such as Ebola, MERS and Zika. The company’s protein-based nanoparticle platform and Matrix-M adjuvant tech can generate vaccine candidates against emerging infectious diseases, already used in marketed COVID-19 and malaria vaccines. Emergent BioSolutions, on the other hand, is often viewed as one of the U.S. government’s primary biodefense and medical-countermeasure contractors during public-health emergencies. The company has existing relationships with BARDA and makes products based on Anthrax, Ebola, smallpox, mpox and viral hemorrhagic fevers. Emergent previously received BARDA task orders for viral hemorrhagic fever therapeutics and has also participated in manufacturing efforts during outbreaks, including Ebola and Zika. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for INO and NVAX was ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume, while MRNA saw ‘bullish’ sentiment with ‘high’ message volume. EBS also recorded ‘extremely bullish’ sentiment, though message volume remained ‘normal.’ Over the past year, MRNA has surged 102%, followed by EBS up 93% and NVAX higher by 55%, while INO has declined 22%. Read Next: SLS Stock Heads For Weekly Win: Deutsche Bank’s Stake Boost Draws Attention Ahead Of Q1 Earnings Datadog is also on track to be the top gainer this week on the Nasdaq 100 and the second-best performer on the S&P 500. In this photo illustration, a smartphone displays the logo of Datadog, Inc.(Photo illustration by Cheng Xin/Getty Images) - Datadog’s customer usage is growing at the fastest rate since early 2022. - Jefferies, Stifel, and Evercore ISI raised their price targets after Q1 earnings. - Jefferies kept a Buy rating, citing the strongest customer usage growth since early 2022. Datadog, Inc.’s stock (DDOG) is on track to notch its best weekly performance on record as the cloud company delivered a breakout first-quarter (Q1) earnings that ignited investor enthusiasm and underscored its key role in the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom. The stock is also set to be the biggest winner this week on the Nasdaq-100 and the second-best performer on the S&P 500. Jefferies, Stifel and Evercore ISI all raised their price targets on Datadog after what analysts broadly described as a solid “beat and raise” quarter. The firms cited stronger-than-anticipated demand, improving guidance and continued momentum in both core and AI-related products. Jefferies raised its price target on DDOG to $210 from $170 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating, according to TheFly. The firm said customer usage grew at its fastest rate since early 2022, showing strong momentum in its main platform services. Stifel made a more aggressive revision, raising its target to $305 from $160 and also reiterating a ‘Buy’ rating. The firm emphasized that revenue growth continued to pick up sequentially. The new price target implies a 61% upside from the stock’s closing price on Thursday. Evercore ISI also raised its price target to $225 from $175, maintaining an Outperform rating. The firm said the company’s quarterly results and forward guidance helped ease concerns that growth might slow later in the year. Datadog stock traded over 1% lower overnight late Thursday, after surging over 31% in the regular session. In Q1, Datadog posted revenue of $1.006 billion, reaching its first-ever billion-dollar mark and beating analyst expectations of $959.9 million. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.60, well above the $0.51 Street forecast, according to Fiscal AI data. The company continued to deepen its enterprise base, growing to roughly 4,550 customers generating more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue, up from about 3,770 a year earlier. Looking ahead, the company sees Q2 revenue between $1.07 billion and $1.08 billion and EPS between $0.57 and $0.59, compared with the Street estimates of $1.06 billion and $0.58, respectively. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory with 1,377% surge in message volume over 24 hours. A user said, “$DDOG earnings just proved high-value SaaS isn’t dying because of AI, it’s accelerating.” Another user said, “damn, I missed this one. Crushing growth with expanding margins.” DDOG stock has gained over 38% year-to-date. Also See: TTD Stock Sinks Overnight On Weak Outlook, But CEO Feels ‘Best Days Are Ahead’ Retail traders said surging cloud demand and the company’s growing order book signaled strong future growth, outweighing concerns around heavy investment for now. The CoreWeave logo is displayed on a mobile phone in this photo illustration in Brussels, Belgium, on November 10, 2025. (Photo by Jonathan Raa/NurPhoto via Getty Images) - CoreWeave’s revenue in Q1 more than doubled and surpassed analysts' expectations; Q2 forecast was softer than expected. - CoreWeave said 2026 capital expenditures would be higher than it had projected earlier. - CRWV stock dropped 10% in post-market hours; retail sentiment moved sharply upward, to ‘extremely bullish.’ CoreWeave, Inc. forecast second-quarter revenue below analysts’ expectations and said its capital expenditure this year would be higher than previously forecast due to increasing component prices, triggering a selloff in shares. Still, retail traders returned upbeat, citing growth prospects and calling the dip an overreaction. CRWV dropped 10% in overnight trading heading into Friday. If the move holds in the regular session, it would mark the worst single-day drop in about a month. CoreWeave’s quarterly report forced investors to reassess their outlook on the company, as strong revenue and order growth were accompanied by sharply rising expenses. In recent months, Meta Platforms committed $21 billion for CoreWeave’s cloud capacity through 2032, with the cloud operator also signing new multi-billion-dollar deals with Anthropic and Jane Street. Demand for the so-called neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius has surged over the last year as tech companies race to secure the hardware and cloud capacity to support AI development and user growth. Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, and Nvidia are among CoreWeave's largest customers. The company’s total revenue surged 105% to $2.08 billion in the first quarter, beating analysts’ estimate of $1.97 billion from LSEG/Reuters. Operating expenses more than doubled to $2.22 billion, a result of continuing to scale active power capacity. Backlog, which denotes orders booked but not yet realized as revenue, jumped to $99.4 billion as of March 31, compared with $66.8 billion at the end of December. Last quarter, CoreWeave added more than 400 megawatts of contracted power, bringing its total to more than 3.5 gigawatts. For Q2, the company expects revenue in the range of $2.45 billion to $2.6 billion, below analysts' estimate of $2.69 billion. The focus item, still, was the capital expenditure. Not only did CoreWeave's capex increased 90% sequentially to $7.70 billion in Q1, but the company also said the 2026 figure would be slightly higher. The company now expects full-year capital expenditures in a range of $31 billion to $35 billion, up from a previous low end of $30 billion. “In the last six, nine months, there has been an acute shortage of certain components that have moved up,” CEO Michael Intrator said on the analyst call, adding that the structure of its supply contracts offers the company some insulation from price volatility. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for CRWV flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ the previous day. “Buying Coreweave now is similar to buying csco in 1989 or cell tower company AMT in 2001 at 1.00,” a trader said, signaling that it's still early days for neocloud companies and the upside potential is huge. “Everybody is worried about today's debt. Well 8 years ago the Oilers gave McDavid 12 million a year. Today that contract looks mighty savy... I think it's bullcrap this stock will be fine with NVDA backing and Blackstone owning notes.” Another wrote: “CoreWeave’s sell-off is a market misread. The business isn’t demand-constrained — the $99.4B backlog proves that.” Still, some traders remained concerned of the growing leverage and bottom-line pressure, with one saying, “losses and debt. This goes below 100 soon enough.” CoreWeave went public in March 2025. The stock has surged 80% this year. Wall Street expects another loss-making quarter, with Koyfin estimates projecting EPS loss to widen to $0.06 from $0.05. SLS stock has surged 188% over the past year. (Photo credit: Getty Images) - Deutsche Bank raised its holdings to 137,646 shares valued at $582,000 in the March quarter. - Sellas’ largest shareholders include Vanguard Group, BlackRock, and State Street, among others. - The company recently took part in discussions on the EU Biotech Act related to drug approvals, biotech competitiveness, and patient access. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences, Inc. (SLS) are poised to end the week in the green as investors increased their bets on the cancer-drug developer and tracked big money ahead of earnings and a potential acute myeloid leukemia (AML) trial catalyst. SLS stock ended Thursday over 4% lower at 4.93, but shares are tracking their best week in nearly a month after gaining about 11% so far this week. Fresh filings showed that Deutsche Bank increased its stake in SLS by 50% during the March quarter. The bank added 45,958 shares, bringing its total holdings to 137,646 shares valued at $582,000, according to data from Quiver Quantitative. The filing came alongside several smaller institutional stakes, including a more than 500% increase from Rothschild Investment, though the stake remains comparatively small at 127 shares. The company’s top shareholders include BlackRock, now the largest investor, with 12.1 million shares valued at $51.3 million as of March 31, up from 7.54 million shares valued at $28.4 million at the end of last year, per Fiscal AI data. As of the end of last year, Vanguard Group held 8.5 million shares valued at $35.8 million. Geode Capital Management held shares valued at about $13 million, while State Street held a stake valued at $9.3 million. Wall Street expects another loss-making quarter as Sellas continues investing heavily in clinical development and pipeline expansion. According to Koyfin estimates, analysts expect a loss per share (EPS) of $0.06 for the quarter, compared with a loss of $0.05 in the prior quarter. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) is projected to widen to $9 million from about $8.3 million previously. According to Koyfin data, Sellas carries a 12-month average analyst price target of $10, implying an upside of 103% from current levels.
