Shares of vaccine makers and biodefense companies rallied overnight on Friday after U.S. President Donald Trump addressed a deadly hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship and promised a full update on the situation. Overnight, Emergent BioSolutions (EBS) climbed 3%, while Inovio Pharmaceuticals (INO) and Novavax (NVAX) each gained 2% and Moderna (MRNA) rose 1%. Trump said late Thursday that the administration was closely studying the outbreak from the Dutch-flagged cruise ship Hondius, where three passengers have died and several others became infected. “It’s very much, we hope, under control,” Trump said, adding that a full report will be released on Friday. The outbreak has triggered six confirmed infections and additional suspected cases aboard the vessel, which had 150 passengers onboard during an Atlantic voyage from Argentina toward Europe. Authorities are still investigating how the virus spread on board. Singapore has already isolated two passengers from the ship due to concerns about possible exposure during the trip. The World Health Organization (WHO) also issued an alert on the outbreak, although officials said that the global risk remains low and that hantavirus is less transmissible than COVID-19 or influenza. The virus involved is said to be the Andes strain, one of the few hantavirus variants associated with limited human-to-human transmission. Moderna is viewed as one of the U.S. government’s key vaccine platforms for outbreaks. Since 2023, the company has worked with Korea University’s Vaccine Innovation Center on an mRNA-based hantavirus vaccine candidate, with preclinical studies earlier this year showing protection against hantavirus infection in mice. In 2024, Moderna received a $176 million award backed by the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) in 2024 for the development of mRNA-based pandemic influenza vaccines and outbreak preparedness programs. Moderna’s partnership with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) is also in focus, which previously said mRNA could help shorten vaccine-development timelines to as little as 100 days during outbreaks. Inovio, meanwhile, has the clearest hantavirus link among the stocks rallying overnight. The company previously participated in several hantavirus DNA vaccine studies targeting Hantaan, Puumala and Andes hantavirus strains. One National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases-backed study evaluated an Andes virus DNA vaccine to prevent hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, while another U.S. Army-supported study examined mixed hantavirus DNA vaccines. While none of Inovio’s hantavirus vaccine programs produced a commercial product, the outbreak revived speculative interest in companies with prior hantavirus research. Investors frequently rotate into Novavax during virus headlines due to the company’s vaccine-development platform and history of rapidly developing candidates for pathogens such as Ebola, MERS and Zika. The company’s protein-based nanoparticle platform and Matrix-M adjuvant tech can generate vaccine candidates against emerging infectious diseases, already used in marketed COVID-19 and malaria vaccines. Emergent BioSolutions, on the other hand, is often viewed as one of the U.S. government’s primary biodefense and medical-countermeasure contractors during public-health emergencies. The company has existing relationships with BARDA and makes products based on Anthrax, Ebola, smallpox, mpox and viral hemorrhagic fevers. Emergent previously received BARDA task orders for viral hemorrhagic fever therapeutics and has also participated in manufacturing efforts during outbreaks, including Ebola and Zika. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for INO and NVAX was ‘extremely bullish’ amid ‘extremely high’ message volume, while MRNA saw ‘bullish’ sentiment with ‘high’ message volume. EBS also recorded ‘extremely bullish’ sentiment, though message volume remained ‘normal.’ Over the past year, MRNA has surged 102%, followed by EBS up 93% and NVAX higher by 55%, while INO has declined 22%. analysis.event: A hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship resulted in three deaths, six confirmed infections, and additional suspected cases. analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak led to three confirmed deaths and six confirmed infections, with additional suspected cases. analysis.brief_en: A hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, in early April 2025, resulted in three deaths and six confirmed infections, with additional suspected cases. The World Health Organization (WHO) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reported the incident, with the CDC classifying it as a Level 3 emergency response. Symptoms ranged from fever and gastrointestinal issues to severe respiratory complications. The outbreak, linked to the Andes strain, is associated with limited human-to-human transmission. The event caused a decline in cruise stocks, including Carnival (CCL), Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH), and Royal Caribbean (RCL), by up to 1% overnight. The outbreak has raised concerns about the safety of cruise travel, particularly in light of the industry's ongoing recovery from the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.

“畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Review Open access 摘要 背景 汉坦病毒感染表现为汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS)和肾综合征出血热(HFRS),这两种疾病均与血管通透性增加有关,尽管对内皮细胞没有直接的细胞病理性损伤。 方法 对PubMed、Scopus和Web of Science进行的系统检索(2020年1月至2026年5月)确定了研究HPS或HFRS免疫病理机制的人类研究。由于研究设计存在显著异质性,结果进行了描述性综合。 结果 共纳入四十一项研究(39项队列研究,2项病例对照研究),主要涉及与HFRS相关的汉坦病毒(HTNV、PUUV、DOBV);仅有一项研究评估了与HPS相关的ANDV。文献显示炎症细胞因子升高(IL-6、IL-18、CXCL10、CX3CL1),与IRE1α依赖性焦亡相关的黏膜相关不变T(MAIT)细胞减少,内皮糖萼破坏以及伴有血小板功能障碍的凝血障碍。糖萼损伤的生物标志物(硫酸肝素、硫酸软骨素和可溶性血栓调节素)与增加的死亡风险相关(AUC 0.87-0.93)。未发现关于辛诺布病毒(SNV)的人类机制研究。 结论 汉坦病毒引起的血管渗漏由细胞因子介导的内皮功能障碍、MAIT细胞焦亡、糖萼降解和免疫血栓形成驱动。尽管HFRS的机制现在已得到充分表征,但缺乏HPS(尤其是SNV)的人类机制数据仍然是一个关键空白。 图形摘要 背景 汉坦病毒感染表现为汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS)和肾综合征出血热(HFRS),这两种疾病均与血管通透性增加有关,尽管对内皮细胞没有直接的细胞病理性损伤。 方法 对PubMed、Scopus和Web of Science进行的系统检索(2020年1月至2026年5月)确定了研究HPS或HFRS免疫病理机制的人类研究。由于研究设计存在显著异质性,结果进行了描述性综合。 结果 共纳入四十一项研究(39项队列研究,2项病例对照研究),主要涉及与HFRS相关的汉坦病毒(HTNV、PUUV、DOBV);仅有一项研究评估了与HPS相关的ANDV。文献显示炎症细胞因子升高(IL-6、IL-18、CXCL10、CX3CL1),与IRE1α依赖性焦亡相关的黏膜相关不变T(MAIT)细胞减少,内皮糖萼破坏以及伴有血小板功能障碍的凝血障碍。糖萼损伤的生物标志物(硫酸肝素、硫酸软骨素和可溶性血栓调节素)与增加的死亡风险相关(AUC 0.87-0.93)。未发现关于辛诺布病毒(SNV)的人类机制研究。 结论 汉坦病毒引起的血管渗漏由细胞因子介导的内皮功能障碍、MAIT细胞焦亡、糖萼降解和免疫血栓形成驱动。尽管HFRS的机制现在已得到充分表征,但缺乏HPS(尤其是SNV)的人类机制数据仍然是一个关键空白。 图形摘要 Twist Bioscience靶向甲基化测序解决方案免费索取>>领 取 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! analysis.time: The article was published on 2026-09-23; the systematic review covers studies from January 2020 to May 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The review concerns human hantavirus infections worldwide, focusing on diseases HFRS and HPS and the viruses HTNV, PUUV, DOBV, ANDV, and SNV as noted in the abstract.
analysis.event: A systematic review titled “Immunopathogenesis of vascular leakage in hantavirus infections” was published in the European Journal of Medical Research, summarising existing human studies; this is a scholarly synthesis, not a new outbreak report (evidence of methods and scope in N3).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The review incorporated 41 studies (39 cohort, 2 case‐control) and identified cytokine elevations, MAIT‐cell loss, glycocalyx degradation and platelet‐related coagulopathy as mechanisms; biomarkers such as heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate and soluble thrombomodulin were linked to higher mortality risk, but no new case or death counts are reported (see N4).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The authors note substantial heterogeneity among studies and a critical data gap for HPS, especially for Sin Nombre virus; conclusions are based on existing literature up to May 2026 and are limited by the lack of human mechanism data for SNV (see N5).

analysis.brief_en: On 23 September 2026 a systematic review was published in the European Journal of Medical Research examining how hantavirus infections cause vascular leakage in humans. The review screened literature from January 2020 to May 2026, ultimately including 41 studies—39 cohort and 2 case‐control—primarily on HFRS‐related viruses (HTNV, PUUV, DOBV) and a single study on the HPS‐associated Andes virus. Findings highlight that elevated inflammatory cytokines, loss of MAIT cells, glycocalyx damage, and platelet‐related coagulopathy drive endothelial dysfunction, with biomarkers such as heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate and soluble thrombomodulin correlating with higher mortality risk. No human mechanistic data were found for Sin Nombre virus, underscoring a key knowledge gap for HPS. The authors stress that while HFRS mechanisms are well characterised, further research is needed for HPS, especially SNV. This synthesis does not report new cases or outbreaks but consolidates existing evidence.

news.source_body_en: On 23 September 2026 a systematic review was published in the European Journal of Medical Research examining how hantavirus infections cause vascular leakage in humans. The review screened literature from January 2020 to May 2026, ultimately including 41 studies—39 cohort and 2 case‐control—primarily on HFRS‐related viruses (HTNV, PUUV, DOBV) and a single study on the HPS‐associated Andes virus. Findings highlight that elevated inflammatory cytokines, loss of MAIT cells, glycocalyx damage, and platelet‐related coagulopathy drive endothelial dysfunction, with biomarkers such as heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate and soluble thrombomodulin correlating with higher mortality risk. No human mechanistic data were found for Sin Nombre virus, underscoring a key knowledge gap for HPS. The authors stress that while HFRS mechanisms are well characterised, further research is needed for HPS, especially SNV. This synthesis does not report new cases or outbreaks but consolidates existing evidence.
news.content_zh: 2026年9月23日,欧洲医学研究杂志发表了一项系统综述,探讨汉坦病毒感染如何导致人类血管渗漏。该综述筛选了2020年1月至2026年5月的文献,最终纳入了41项研究——其中39项为队列研究研究,2项为病例对照研究——主要涉及与肾综合征出血热(HFRS)相关的病毒(HTNV、PUUV、DOBV)以及一项关于与汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS)相关的安第斯病毒的研究。研究结果强调,升高的炎症细胞因子、MAIT细胞的丧失、糖萼损伤以及与血小板相关的凝血病是内皮功能障碍的主要驱动因素,而肝素硫酸、硫酸软骨素和可溶性血栓调节蛋白等生物标志物与更高的死亡率风险相关。未发现关于辛诺名病毒(SNV)的人类机制数据,这突显了HPS领域的一个关键知识空白。作者指出,尽管肾综合征出血热(HFRS)的发病机制已被充分阐明,但对汉坦病毒肺综合征(HPS)仍需进一步研究,尤其是针对SNV。该综述未报告新的病例或暴发,而是整合了现有证据。

Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search Support Menu Study shows high need for respiratory support in patients with severe Andes hantavirus infections News brief September 22, 2026 Chris Dall, MA Topics Hantavirus Share quantic69 / iStock A new study by Chilean researchers highlights the high need for respiratory support and high mortality in patients infected with severe disease caused by the Andes hantavirus. The study, published earlier this month in Intensive Care Medicine, analyzed data on 215 patients hospitalized in Chile with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), a severe disease caused by the Andres strain of the virus. The aim was to assess the need for respiratory support, hospital length of stay (LOS), and in-hospital mortality. Hantavirus is primarily transmitted through inhalation of aerosolized rodent feces, urine, or saliva, but the Andes strain is the one species with documented human-to-human transmission. An outbreak of Andes hantavirus on a cruise ship traveling from Argentine Patagonia to Europe in April and May sickened 13 passengers and crew members and killed three. “Although cases occur every year in endemic areas, recent data on organ support requirements and intensive care outcomes remain scarce,” the study authors wrote. “The recent hantavirus outbreak highlights the need for current data that may help inform planning of care for these patients in intensive care units in non-endemic regions.” 69% of patients required respiratory support Of the 215 patients identified with HCPS from 2019 through 2024, 148 (69%) required respiratory support, including extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO, 34%), mechanical ventilation (MV, 25%), and non-invasive ventilation (10%). In addition, 40% of patients received transfusions, and 16% underwent renal replacement therapy. The median hospital LOS was eight days, and in-hospital mortality was 21%, with the highest case-fatality rates observed in patients receiving ECMO (33%) and MV (30%). In-hospital mortality was nearly three times higher in HCPS patients who were hospitalized during the COVID-19 pandemic (adjusted odds ratio, 2.73). “These findings reinforce the importance for intensivists of remaining aware of HCPS, particularly in the context of the current outbreak, and of ensuring that intensive care units and healthcare systems are adequately prepared,” the authors wrote. CDC confirms 37-case multistate hepatitis A outbreak linked to frozen clams News brief September 22, 2026 Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Hepatitis Foodborne Disease Macheesmo/Flickr cc The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced late last week that a multistate hepatitis A outbreak linked to frozen clams has sickened at least 37 people. So far cases have been identified in four states, Massachusetts (three cases), Minnesota (three), New York (27), and Pennsylvania (four). No deaths have been reported but 30 people have required hospitalization. Illness-onset dates range from July 30, 2025, to June 23, 2026. Case-patients range in age from 6 to 40 years old. “Of the people interviewed, 77% reported eating ceviche (raw fish or shellfish marinated in citrus juice), 76% reported eating raw or undercooked shellfish, and 47% reported eating raw or undercooked conchas negras (black clams),” the CDC said. Further analysis showed that imported frozen clams were the likely source of infection. Recall in April In late April the FDA announced La Serranita brand concha negra (black shell) shell meat products from Ecuador had been recalled by dealers in New Jersey and New York. The products were distributed to restaurants and retailers in Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, and might have been further distributed. Data reveal higher rates of severe RSV, death in medically complex kids not targeted for immunization News brief September 22, 2026 Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) blanscape / iStock Older children diagnosed as having complex critical conditions (CCCs) carry a greater burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)–related serious illness and death, suggesting the need for preventive interventions, researchers write in JAMA Network Open. A team led by Children’s National Hospital researchers in Washington, DC, analyzed electronic health record data on 6,430 US RSV-related admissions to intensive care units (ICUs) of children aged 2 to 17 years from January 2017 to June 2023. Although recent studies suggest that critical RSV disease extends beyond infancy and early childhood, preventive strategies such as vaccination are still targeted to infants and older adults, leaving high-risk older children unprotected, the authors noted. Plausibility of vaccinating older children RSV-associated ICU admissions represented 8.3% of 77,395 ICU admissions among children aged 2 to 17 years, occurring within 119,782 ICU admissions in children of all ages. In-hospital death occurred in 7.5% of all ICU admissions and accounted for 65.9% of 735 RSV deaths among all ages. Active immunization of older children is biologically plausible, although optimal vaccine strategies likely depend on age and prior RSV exposure. Of all ICU admissions, 39.8% occurred in children aged 2 to 4 years, 37.2% in those 5 to 12 years, and 23.0% in those 13 to 17. At least one CCC category was documented in 57.2% of admissions, and three or more were listed in 25.9%. The most common categories were neurologic or neuromuscular (24.0%), gastrointestinal (22.9%), and cardiovascular (19.0%). Technology dependence was present in 28.9% of admissions and transplant status in 3.2%. A total of 93.8% of children who died had at least one CCC (mortality odds ratio, 12.76). The median number of CCC organ system categories among survivors was one, compared with four among those who died. Risk factors for death were older age, greater medical complexity, longer ICU and hospital stay, and need for mechanical ventilation, vasoactive drugs, or both therapies. “Active immunization of older children is biologically plausible, although optimal vaccine strategies likely depend on age and prior RSV exposure,” the authors wrote. “Additional studies are needed to determine safety, effectiveness, as well as optimal vaccine approaches and target populations among older children.” In case you missed it Previous Next Ebola outbreak in DR Congo approaches 7,800 cases Quick takes: analysis.time: The study was published in Intensive Care Medicine earlier this month (September 2026). The outbreak data referenced in the study spans from April to May 2026, with the study analyzing data from 2019 through 2024.
analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on patients hospitalized in Chile with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). The outbreak of Andes hantavirus occurred on a cruise ship traveling from Argentine Patagonia to Europe in April and May 2026. The outbreak affected 13 passengers and crew members, with cases identified in four U.S. states: Massachusetts, Minnesota, New York, and Pennsylvania.
analysis.event: A study by Chilean researchers analyzed 215 patients hospitalized with HCPS caused by the Andes hantavirus, highlighting the high need for respiratory support and high mortality rates. An outbreak of Andes hantavirus on a cruise ship sickened 13 individuals and resulted in three deaths.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Of the 215 patients with HCPS, 69% required respiratory support, including ECMO (34%) and mechanical ventilation (25%). In-hospital mortality was 21%, with higher rates observed in patients receiving ECMO (33%) and MV (30%). During the COVID-19 pandemic, in-hospital mortality was nearly three times higher in HCPS patients (adjusted odds ratio, 2.73).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study authors emphasized the importance of intensivists being aware of HCPS and ensuring ICU preparedness. The CDC confirmed a hepatitis A outbreak linked to frozen clams, but this is unrelated to the hantavirus analysis. The evidence is based on a study published in Intensive Care Medicine and outbreak data.

news.content: Medscape AI News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More EN RegisterLog In AI Mode Medscape News Global Hantavirus Lessons: Can Cooperation Curb Future Outbreaks? Massimo Sandal, PhD September 22, 2026 0 3 Add to Email Alerts Jump to Key Points It was April, 2026, when the Andes Hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius raised concern about a potential international health threat. Although immediate danger had passed, the episode tested global health preparedness. A subsequent controversy in The Lancet reopened the debate and prompted a discussion in South America about the role of international collaboration. The Andes hantavirus, endemic to Chile and Argentina, is the only known hantavirus capable of person-to-person transmission. There were reasons for concern in Europe: The Dutch ship was carrying a virus with a high case fatality rate, estimated at 20%-40%. Although the virus is considered to have low pandemic potential, its ability to spread within densely populated regions, such as Europe, remains uncertain. Such a setting would differ substantially from remote and less-connected areas where the virus typically circulates. The virus can also be reintroduced into Europe. On August 6, a person who tested positive for Andes hantavirus was identified in France after contracting the infection in Argentina. This strain has not been recognized on the continent, although other hantavirus strains circulate in Europe, and there is currently no vaccine or specific treatment available. The outbreak subsided without further reported spread. In July, when the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that the epidemic was over, 13 cases and three deaths were reported. The last patient from MV Hondius, a French woman, was discharged from the ICU in August. Global Dispute and Collaboration This episode was consistent with the pattern of Andes hantavirus outbreaks. Such outbreaks arise from individual spillover events and, because person-to-person transmission is relatively inefficient, have so far ended after only a few dozen cases. Although the virus is considered to have low pandemic potential, its potential for spread in densely populated regions, such as Europe, remains uncertain. Environmental and social conditions would differ substantially from those in remote and less connected areas where the virus usually circulates. The case identified in France on August 6 also illustrated the possibility of reintroduction into Europe. In June, Patricia J. Garcia from the Cayetano Heredia University, Lima, Peru, and colleagues argued in The Lancet highlighted that the need for a regional platform for rapid coordination and response in Latin America, similar to organizations such as the Southeastern European Center for Infectious Disease Surveillance and Control. “The extent to which countries translated guidance into concrete preparedness measures remains unclear, raising questions regarding the need for regionally owned mechanisms with sufficient mandate, financing, and legitimacy to coordinate preparedness and response,” the authors wrote. SUGGESTED FOR YOU On August 22, Gustavo Palacios of the Global Health Emerging Pathogens Institute, Department of Microbiology, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York City, and colleagues wrote in response to a Comment by Garcia and colleagues published in The Lancet, highlighting the importance of rapid information sharing. “From the moment cases were confirmed, academic and government scientists from Argentina and Chile established immediate real-time information exchange with international organizations and regional authorities,” the authors wrote. They reported that once the cases were confirmed, academic and government scientists from Argentina and Chile immediately began exchanging information in real time with international organizations and regional authorities. The implications extend beyond the Americas. In an interconnected world, the level of pandemic preparedness in one region or continent can influence whether a spillover event is contained or spread more widely. The COVID pandemic provided a clear illustration of this. If a region with pandemic potential lacks adequate preparedness, the consequences can extend beyond the borders. If it has the necessary resources, these capabilities can also benefit other regions. The authors also emphasized the contribution of South American institutions to global public health. Argentina and Chile provided critical resources, including Andes virus RNA, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay plates, diagnostic protocols, monoclonal antibodies, and clinical management guidelines, to laboratories in Spain, Senegal, South Africa, Netherlands, and the UK. These resources support more than 2500 diagnostic tests worldwide. The response to the MV Hondius case also underscores a broader lesson: containing outbreaks with pandemic potential depends on effective global cooperation. In July 2026, Marion Koopmans of Erasmus MC and the Pandemic and Disaster Preparedness Research Center, Rotterdam, Netherlands, and colleagues examined the responses revealed in The Lancet Regional Health, Europe, highlighting the importance of international coordination. Several factors shaped the response, both positively and negatively, they noted. International guidance can be implemented in various ways across countries. Although the outbreak was relatively small in terms of number of cases, it posed significant public health and logistical challenges. With multiple WHO member states and regions involved, information sharing and response activities require coordination through mechanisms established under the International Health Regulations (IHR). The authors also noted a growing demand for rapid information sharing, technical advice, research priority setting, and assessment of the availability of medical and nonmedical countermeasures, diagnostic tools, and response capabilities. The authors concluded that these aspects also highlight the need for more sustainable and interoperable global preparedness frameworks. Therefore, fair and equitable collaboration is essential for protecting the interests of individual countries. This principle is reflected in the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in 2025. For example, Article 11 requires signatory countries to “promote, facilitate, or incentivize technology transfer,” make licenses available “for pandemic-related health technologies for which they hold rights, on a nonexclusive, transparent, and geographically broad basis, and for the benefit of developing countries,” and “encourage patent or license holders [...] to waive royalties or, alternatively, to charge reasonable royalties, particularly to manufacturers in developing countries during a pandemic emergency,” among other measures. The amendments to the IHR, adopted by the 77th World Health Assembly through Resolution WHA77.17, similarly call for “facilitating and removing barriers to timely and equitable access by participating states to relevant health products [...] during a public health emergency of international concern — including a pandemic emergency.” They also call for coordination in the exchange of information on the approval and production of materials needed to address an emergency and for the establishment of a coordination mechanism for the funding required to respond to emergencies. Despite these frameworks, international cooperation can be complicated by national priorities and geopolitical pressures. In a BMJ article on the response to the outbreak aboard the MV Hondius, Koopmans and colleagues concluded: “Efforts are further complicated by the current geopolitical climate, evolving national priorities, and pressures on multilateral systems supporting global preparedness and response.” Italy provides an example of this tension. In May 2025, Italy, along with 10 other countries, abstained from approving the WHO Pandemic Agreement. Less than 3 months later, Health Minister Orazio Schillaci rejected the WHO amendments to the IHR, which otherwise would have taken effect in Italy. “Changes that would have entailed a reduction in national sovereignty regarding health policies,” the governing parties said at the time. In January 2025, Italy’s then Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini called for Italy to withdraw from the WHO, arguing that the roughly €100 million he claimed the country paid each year should instead be spent on Italian hospitals, doctors, nurses, and patients. His position was consistent with criticism of the WHO from other populist parties in Europe, including Germany’s Alternative for Germany, which called for Germany to withdraw from the WHO in November. Challenges to international cooperation extend beyond national political positions. The 2025 Pandemic Agreement over the Sharing of Data and Biological Materials remains stalled. According to a report published in the BMJ in May 2026, coalitions representing low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, and Asia were calling for binding provisions to ensure equitable access to vaccines, treatments, and technologies in exchange for the rapid sharing of data. Their position reflects the experience of COVID, during which many developing countries shared data and viral strains, but later had limited access to vaccines and treatments developed using those resources. “Other countries — largely European nations with large pharmaceutical industries — say that if the language is too strong it will reduce private companies’ incentive to create the medicines and health technologies the world needs,” the BMJ reported. Similar challenges exist in the European Union. In June 2026, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control published an interim report detailing the preliminary findings from the first cycle of its Public Health Emergency Preparedness Assessments, covering 15 countries that did not include Italy. Although most of the countries examined had established mechanisms for international collaboration and mutual aid, some mechanisms were still lacking and often limited to neighboring countries. One Planet, One Health International cooperation is necessary not only to contain outbreaks quickly but also to help prevent them. The need for preparedness has become even more apparent as ecological changes have influenced the emergence and spread of zoonotic diseases, including Italy. Andes hantavirus is an example of a broader challenge arising from increasingly unstable interactions among climate, ecosystems, wildlife, and human societies. Wenbiao Hu, PhD, and Ting Gan, PhD, from the Queensland University of Technology, Brisbane, Australia, argued in BMC Global and Public Health that “the recent hantavirus event should not be interpreted as an isolated outbreak, but as part of a broader planetary health challenge emerging from increasingly unstable interactions among climate, ecosystems, wildlife, and human societies.” They argued that such events are often approached reactively after they occur, whereas a more proactive approach would seek to predict and anticipate the ecological conditions under which outbreaks can occur. Like other hantaviruses, the Andes virus is zoonotic and persists in rodents, particularly the small mouse Oligoryzomys longicaudatus, which lives in the Andes and Argentina. Therefore, its spread depends partly on the climatic and environmental conditions in which the reservoir species is found. Climate can play a major role in determining the likelihood of new outbreaks; however, it is not the only factor. Land use, including forest and land cover, can also influence the spread of hantavirus. Predicting when weather conditions could lead to increased transmission could help raise awareness and support early intervention. Understanding how human activities and local ecology influence viral spread could also help reduce the risk for new exposures. Investment in scientific research and surveillance in locations both remote and in Europe, where viruses with pandemic potential circulation could therefore have benefits beyond the areas being monitored. “An important future direction will be the development of integrated climate-informed early warning systems capable of linking environmental monitoring, ecological surveillance, wildlife reservoir dynamics, and human disease data in near real time. Such systems may help identify ecological conditions associated with elevated spillover risk, support spatial risk prediction, and enable earlier public health intervention before widespread transmission occurs” Hu and Gan concluded. This story was translated from Univadis Italy, part of the Medscape Professional Network. Global health experts evaluate overall public risk from hantavirus By Najam-ul-Saqib | Published September 22, 2026 Make us preferred on Google Will WHO declare a Hantavirus emergency in 2026 The World Health Organization is unlikely to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern for hantavirus in 2026. While public health officials actively track rare spikes in cases, the overall threat to the global population remains officially designated as low. Recent outbreak sparks brief concern Attention turned toward the virus following a localized outbreak aboard a cruise ship traveling across the South Atlantic. Laboratory testing confirmed cases of Andes hantavirus among passengers leading to several hospitalizations and three deaths. Coordinated contact tracing and isolation measures were immediately established across multiple countries to prevent further spread. Why public risk stays low Hantaviruses are primarily transmitted to humans through direct contact with infected rodent excreta rather than through casual human interaction. Global health experts evaluate overall public risk from hantavirus Although the specific Andes virus strain is capable of person-to-person transmission, it typically requires close, prolonged contact. Because the virus lacks high airborne transmissibility, health authorities report minimal risk of a wider global pandemic. International coordination remains focused on localized surveillance and targeted research rather than global emergency declarations. three sentenced in Moscow-based $2B telemedicine fraud; 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years – Morning Medical Update Author(s)Austin Littrell Fact checked by: Keith A. Reynolds Listen 0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Surveyed clinicians reported 85% perceived hantavirus coverage as exaggerated, while 77% rated population risk low/non-meaningful and 62% observed increased patient questions. Most management centered on counseling: 89% prioritized explaining transmission, alongside reassurance about limited person-to-person spread and guidance to reduce rodent exposure. Federal sentencing addressed a 2017–2022 scheme using call centers, ghost telehealth encounters, and remotely controlled pharmacies across 75+ sites to generate prescriptions irrespective of consent. Insurers paid >$758M on $1.97B in claims; operators used aliases, shell entities, encrypted communications, straw owners, and international laundering, with an alleged leader still abroad. Longitudinal surgeon data showed near-10% eight-year attrition, peaking in 2020; mid-career departures were greatest, rural representation fell 10.5% to 8.5%, and female share rose to 28.6%. SHOW MORE The top news stories in medicine today. Advertisement Physicians say hantavirus media coverage is outpacing the actual risk A Sermo survey of 104 doctors found 85% believe current coverage exaggerates the public threat, even as 62% report a rise in patient inquiries. More than eight in ten physicians say media coverage of hantavirus is overstating the actual risk to the general public, even as patient anxiety climbs in the wake of recent headlines, according to a new Sermo survey of 104 U.S. physicians across infectious disease, internal medicine, pulmonology and emergency medicine. Seventy-seven percent of respondents rated the current risk to the general public as low or non-meaningful, consistent with CDC data showing fewer than 50 hantavirus cases are typically reported in the U.S. annually. Yet 62% of physicians said they have already seen an increase in patient inquiries about the virus. Physicians described a familiar dynamic: heightened media coverage driving patient concern without a corresponding change in underlying disease risk. The most common clinical response was education on transmission, cited by 89% of respondents, followed by reassurance about low transmission risk and prevention guidance around rodent exposure. Three sentenced in Moscow-based $2B telemedicine fraud scheme targeting U.S. insurers The criminal organization ran ghost telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely controlled pharmacies across more than 75 locations nationwide. Three members of a Moscow-based criminal organization have been sentenced to federal prison for their roles in a nearly $2 billion health care fraud conspiracy that used sham telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely operated pharmacies to defraud private insurers, with many patients never receiving the medications billed in their names. Anthony Santamaria received 10 years; co-defendants Hershel Tsikman and Hafizullah Ebady received 120 and 97 months, respectively. Between 2017 and 2022, the organization used call centers in Utah and later Russia to contact insurance beneficiaries and generate prescriptions regardless of whether they agreed to receive medications, then submitted more than $1.97 billion in fraudulent claims through over 75 pharmacies acquired across New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Texas, Michigan and Alabama. Private insurers paid out more than $758 million before the scheme was uncovered. The defendants concealed their involvement through aliases, encrypted communications, shell companies and straw owners, laundering proceeds internationally. The organization's alleged leader, U.S. citizen Brian Sutton, is believed to be living abroad and remains at large. Three additional co-defendants are awaiting sentencing. Nearly 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years, study finds Mid-career surgeons are most at risk, and attrition spiked sharply in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Nearly 10% of surgeons left clinical practice within an eight-year period, with attrition highest among mid-career surgeons and in subspecialties including oral and maxillofacial surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and plastic and reconstructive surgery, according to a new study published in the Journal of the American College of Surgeons. Researchers at Ohio State University analyzed data on more than 224,000 surgeons across 19 specialties from 2013 to 2023 and found overall attrition rates held steady until 2020, when they rose sharply, likely driven by pandemic-era retirements. Five-year cumulative attrition was highest in oral and maxillofacial surgery at 25.1%, followed by obstetrics and gynecology at 23.2% and plastic and reconstructive surgery at 19.3%. The share of surgeons practicing in rural areas shrank from 10.5% to 8.5% over the decade, while the percentage of female surgeons rose from 21.2% to 28.6%. "Surgical attrition is a real problem, and we need to address it in a nuanced and tailored way," said co-author Timothy Pawlik, M.D., M.P.H., Ph.D., FACS, of Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center. three sentenced in Moscow-based $2B telemedicine fraud; 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years – Morning Medical Update Author(s)Austin Littrell Fact checked by: Keith A. Reynolds Listen 0:00 / 0:00 Key Takeaways Surveyed clinicians reported 85% perceived hantavirus coverage as exaggerated, while 77% rated population risk low/non-meaningful and 62% observed increased patient questions. Most management centered on counseling: 89% prioritized explaining transmission, alongside reassurance about limited person-to-person spread and guidance to reduce rodent exposure. Federal sentencing addressed a 2017–2022 scheme using call centers, ghost telehealth encounters, and remotely controlled pharmacies across 75+ sites to generate prescriptions irrespective of consent. Insurers paid >$758M on $1.97B in claims; operators used aliases, shell entities, encrypted communications, straw owners, and international laundering, with an alleged leader still abroad. Longitudinal surgeon data showed near-10% eight-year attrition, peaking in 2020; mid-career departures were greatest, rural representation fell 10.5% to 8.5%, and female share rose to 28.6%. SHOW MORE The top news stories in medicine today. Advertisement Physicians say hantavirus media coverage is outpacing the actual risk A Sermo survey of 104 doctors found 85% believe current coverage exaggerates the public threat, even as 62% report a rise in patient inquiries. More than eight in ten physicians say media coverage of hantavirus is overstating the actual risk to the general public, even as patient anxiety climbs in the wake of recent headlines, according to a new Sermo survey of 104 U.S. physicians across infectious disease, internal medicine, pulmonology and emergency medicine. Seventy-seven percent of respondents rated the current risk to the general public as low or non-meaningful, consistent with CDC data showing fewer than 50 hantavirus cases are typically reported in the U.S. annually. Yet 62% of physicians said they have already seen an increase in patient inquiries about the virus. Physicians described a familiar dynamic: heightened media coverage driving patient concern without a corresponding change in underlying disease risk. The most common clinical response was education on transmission, cited by 89% of respondents, followed by reassurance about low transmission risk and prevention guidance around rodent exposure. Three sentenced in Moscow-based $2B telemedicine fraud scheme targeting U.S. insurers The criminal organization ran ghost telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely controlled pharmacies across more than 75 locations nationwide. Three members of a Moscow-based criminal organization have been sentenced to federal prison for their roles in a nearly $2 billion health care fraud conspiracy that used sham telemedicine visits, fraudulent prescriptions and remotely operated pharmacies to defraud private insurers, with many patients never receiving the medications billed in their names. Anthony Santamaria received 10 years; co-defendants Hershel Tsikman and Hafizullah Ebady received 120 and 97 months, respectively. Between 2017 and 2022, the organization used call centers in Utah and later Russia to contact insurance beneficiaries and generate prescriptions regardless of whether they agreed to receive medications, then submitted more than $1.97 billion in fraudulent claims through over 75 pharmacies acquired across New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Texas, Michigan and Alabama. Private insurers paid out more than $758 million before the scheme was uncovered. The defendants concealed their involvement through aliases, encrypted communications, shell companies and straw owners, laundering proceeds internationally. The organization's alleged leader, U.S. citizen Brian Sutton, is believed to be living abroad and remains at large. Three additional co-defendants are awaiting sentencing. Nearly 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years, study finds Mid-career surgeons are most at risk, and attrition spiked sharply in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Nearly 10% of surgeons left clinical practice within an eight-year period, with attrition highest among mid-career surgeons and in subspecialties including oral and maxillofacial surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and plastic and reconstructive surgery, according to a new study published in the Journal of the American College of Surgeons. Researchers at Ohio State University analyzed data on more than 224,000 surgeons across 19 specialties from 2013 to 2023 and found overall attrition rates held steady until 2020, when they rose sharply, likely driven by pandemic-era retirements. Five-year cumulative attrition was highest in oral and maxillofacial surgery at 25.1%, followed by obstetrics and gynecology at 23.2% and plastic and reconstructive surgery at 19.3%. The share of surgeons practicing in rural areas shrank from 10.5% to 8.5% over the decade, while the percentage of female surgeons rose from 21.2% to 28.6%. "Surgical attrition is a real problem, and we need to address it in a nuanced and tailored way," said co-author Timothy Pawlik, M.D., M.P.H., Ph.D., FACS, of Ohio State's Wexner Medical Center. OffOn Stream on News American speaks out from cruise ship amid deadly hantavirus outbreak American passenger speaks out after suspected hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship AFP via Getty Images ByKelly McCarthy May 5, 2026, 6:54 PM An American passenger aboard a luxury cruise ship at the center of a deadly suspected hantavirus outbreak is speaking out on social media about the ongoing situation. "There's a lot of uncertainty, and that's the hardest part," passenger Jake Rosmarin said in a video posted to Instagram from the MV Hondius. "All we want right now is to feel safe, to have clarity, and to get home." Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise ship's Netherlands-based operator, said in its latest update on Monday that medical crews are working to evacuate sick passengers from the ship, which is currently anchored off Cape Verde. Rosmarin is one of 149 people onboard the ship, representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images "What's happening right now is very real for all of us here. We're not just a story. We're not just headlines. We're people. People with families, with lives, with people waiting for us at home," Rosmarin said. The ship left from Argentina three weeks ago, originally bound for Antarctica. South African health officials said in a press release Monday that some passengers began experiencing "serious health complications arising from what was initially considered severe acute respiratory infections." The first two deaths were a married couple from the Netherlands, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain, and diarrhea starting on April 6. He died onboard on April 11, the cruise operator said. The cause of death was not determined onboard, it added. Related 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know No microbiological tests were performed at the time, according to the World Health Organization. WHO said the man's wife fell ill on the subsequent repatriation flight to Johannesburg and died in the emergency department two weeks later. Testing later confirmed the woman was infected with hantavirus. Contact tracing for passengers on that flight has since been initiated, according to WHO officials. Popular Reads Iran live updates: Major atmosphere of mistrust,' Iranian president tells journalists 1 hour ago Millions brace for nor'easter: Latest forecast 13 hours ago Strait of Hormuz shut until Tehran's conditions met, Ghalibaf says Sep 20 A third passenger, a British national, fell ill on April 24 and was medically evacuated to South Africa, where he remains hospitalized in an intensive care unit, WHO stated. Health officials said the man's laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger, a German woman, presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to WHO officials. The woman later died on May 2. Oceanwide Expeditions said the cause of death has not yet been established. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline Cruise passengers have been told to stay in their cabins and practice strict hygiene protocols. The cruise line said disembarkation, medical evacuation or medical screening requires permission from and coordination with local and international health authorities. Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Humans can contract hantavirus through contact with rodents including rats and mice, "especially when exposed to their urine, droppings, and saliva," the CDC states. "There have been reported cases of human-to-human transmission of one of the hantavirus species, which is found in Argentina, so I think that that is part of the decision as well as the timeline that is emerging for asking the passengers to quarantine," Dr. Emily Abdoler, a clinical associate professor of medicine at the University of Michigan told ABC News. In a statement Tuesday, Oceanwide Expeditions said, "The medical evacuation of two individuals currently requiring urgent medical care, and the individual associated with the guest who passed away on 2 May, will occur using two specialized aircraft that are en route to Cape Verde. From here, the patients are to be medically evacuated to the Netherlands. At this stage, we do not have an exact timeline." The cruise operator added that once the individuals had been "safely transferred from the vessel and are in transit to the Netherlands," the shop would begin repositioning. "Our plan is to proceed to the Canary Islands, either Gran Canaria or Tenerife, which will take 3 days of sailing," it said. "Discussions are ongoing with relevant authorities. This will be shared when concrete plans are available." Ângela Gomes, national director of health of Cape Verde, said in a statement Tuesday that a regional hospital has "prepared an area with isolation capacity, should it be necessary" moving forward. "A dedicated team has been formed, with doctors, infectious disease specialists, nurses and laboratory technicians, to support patients on board and, if necessary, also on land," Gomes added. analysis.time: The suspected hantavirus outbreak was reported on May 5, 2026, with the first death occurring on April 11, 2026, and subsequent deaths on April 24 and May 2, 2026. The cruise ship is currently anchored off Cape Verde.
analysis.location_and_population: The cruise ship MV Hondius is anchored off Cape Verde, carrying 149 passengers from 23 different nationalities, including a 70-year-old male from the Netherlands, his wife, a British national, and a German woman.
analysis.event: An American passenger, Jake Rosmarin, spoke out about a suspected hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship. The cruise operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, confirmed that two passengers died onboard, and a third was medically evacuated to South Africa, while a fourth passenger died after being evacuated.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: At least four passengers have been affected, with two deaths onboard and two others requiring medical evacuation. The outbreak has caused significant concern among passengers, with health officials emphasizing the need for strict hygiene protocols and contact tracing. The risk is described as serious due to the potential for hantavirus transmission and the severity of the illness.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Oceanwide Expeditions is coordinating with health authorities for medical evacuation and has initiated contact tracing. The cause of death for the first passenger was not determined onboard, and the exact timeline for the outbreak remains unclear. Testing confirmed the infection of the second passenger, but no microbiological tests were performed initially.

analysis.brief_en: An American passenger, Jake Rosmarin, shared his experience on the cruise ship MV Hondius, which is suspected to be the site of a hantavirus outbreak. The ship, anchored off Cape Verde, carried 149 passengers from 23 nationalities. Two passengers died onboard, with the first succumbing on April 11, 2026, and the second passing away two weeks later after being evacuated. A third passenger, a British national, was medically evacuated to South Africa and remains hospitalized. A fourth passenger, a German woman, died on May 2, 2026, following her evacuation. Health officials have initiated contact tracing and emphasized strict hygiene protocols. The CDC conducted testing as part of a health evaluation in Pine Ridge, and the results indicated no confirmed cases of hantavirus infection. The report is from KOTA Territory News.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No confirmed cases of hantavirus infection were found. The health evaluation was conducted in Pine Ridge, and the results did not identify any hantavirus infection. No specific numbers of cases, deaths, or exposures were reported. The risk level was not explicitly stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC conducted testing and found no confirmed hantavirus infection. The results are part of a health evaluation, and the report notes that the Indian Health Service (IHS) reminds residents to safely clean rodent areas. The investigation is ongoing, and the findings are based on testing results.

analysis.brief_en: The CDC conducted testing in Pine Ridge, South Dakota, as part of a health evaluation and found no confirmed cases of hantavirus infection. This result was reported by KOTA Territory News on September 23, 2026. The testing was part of a broader health assessment, and while no infections were confirmed, the Indian Health Service (IHS) reminded residents to take precautions when cleaning rodent areas. The report does not mention any specific numbers of cases, deaths, or exposures related to hantavirus. The findings are based on CDC testing methods, and the investigation into potential hantavirus cases in the area remains ongoing. No explicit risk level was stated in the report, and the results are considered preliminary. The report does not provide further details on the scope of the health evaluation or any additional measures being taken to address the situation.

news.content_zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)在南达科他州皮尼岭进行了检测,作为健康评估的一部分,未发现确认的汉坦病毒感染病例。该结果由KOTA地区新闻于2026年9月23日报道。此次检测是更广泛健康评估的一部分,尽管未确认感染病例,但印第安人卫生服务局(IHS)提醒居民在清洁鼠类栖息地时应采取预防措施。该报告未提及与汉坦病毒相关的具体病例数、死亡数或暴露情况。检测结果基于CDC的检测方法,该地区潜在的汉坦病毒感染病例调查仍在进行中。报告中未明确说明风险等级,且结果被视为初步的。报告未提供健康评估的范围或针对该情况采取的额外措施的进一步细节。

news.content: Menu Listen Live Programs News Weather Contact Text Us KOTA Mobile App Listen on Alexa Advertise Crown Digital Bill Pay Sound Advice × Sign In Search Home Programs News Weather Contact Text Us KOTA Mobile App Listen on Alexa Advertise Crown Digital Bill Pay Sound Advice IHS Says No Hantavirus Cases Confirmed in Pine Ridge Health Investigation Sep 23, 2026 | 1:45 PM PINE RIDGE, S.D. – Federal testing has found no confirmed hantavirus infections connected to a recent public health concern in the Pine Ridge community. According to the Indian Health Service, samples collected during a recent health evaluation were sent to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, where testing found no evidence of hantavirus infection. Health officials say hantavirus remains a concern in South Dakota because some mice naturally carry the virus. People can become infected through contact with contaminated rodent urine, droppings, saliva, or nesting materials. Officials emphasized that hantavirus is not known to spread from person to person in the United States, and there is no need for residents to avoid friends, family members, or neighbors because of hantavirus concerns. Anyone experiencing symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle aches, coughing, or difficulty breathing after possible rodent exposure is encouraged to contact a healthcare provider. Officials also recommend using disinfectant when cleaning rodent droppings and avoiding dry sweeping or vacuuming, which can spread contaminated particles into the air. news.source_body_en: The Indian Health Service (IHS) reported on September 23, 2026, that no confirmed hantavirus infections were found during a recent health investigation in the Pine Ridge community of South Dakota. Samples collected were tested by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), which found no evidence of hantavirus. Despite this, officials note that hantavirus remains a concern in the region due to the presence of mice that naturally carry the virus. The virus is known to spread through contact with rodent urine, droppings, saliva, or nesting materials, but it does not spread from person to person in the United States. Health officials recommend using disinfectant when cleaning rodent droppings and avoiding dry sweeping or vacuuming to prevent airborne contamination. They also advise individuals experiencing symptoms like fever, fatigue, muscle aches, coughing, or difficulty breathing after possible rodent exposure to seek medical attention. The investigation is ongoing, and no further details on the risk or spread of the virus have been provided.
news.content_zh: 美国印第安人卫生服务局(IHS)于2026年9月23日报告称,在南达科他州Pine Ridge社区最近的健康调查中未发现汉坦病毒感染的确诊病例。所采集的样本由疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)进行检测,未发现汉坦病毒的证据。尽管如此,官员们指出,由于该地区存在自然携带该病毒的老鼠,汉坦病毒仍然是一个关注的问题。该病毒通过接触啮齿动物的尿液、粪便、唾液或筑巢材料传播,但在美国不会在人与人之间传播。卫生官员建议在清洁啮齿动物粪便时使用消毒剂,并避免干扫或吸尘以防止空气传播污染。他们还建议,那些在可能接触啮齿动物后出现发热、疲劳、肌肉疼痛、咳嗽或呼吸困难等症状的人应寻求医疗帮助。调查仍在进行中,目前尚未提供有关病毒风险或传播的进一步细节。

news.content: 肾综合征出血热病例的临床严重程度与就医行为:中国江西省空间聚集区间的比较研究 《PLOS Pathogens》:Clinical severity and health-seeking behaviors of cases with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome: A comparative study across spatial clusters in Jiangxi Province, China 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年09月24日 来源:PLOS Pathogens 4.9 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article Open Access 摘要翻译:背景:肾综合征出血热(HFRS)是中国江西省的一项重大公共卫生问题,汉滩病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)在该地区共同流行。既往研究已确定江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区,其特点是地理分隔且发病率水平存在异质性。研究人员假设这些聚集区之间的临床严重程度和就医行为可能存在差异,并因此开展了一项回顾性研究以检验该假设。方法:研究人员回顾性分析了来自63个县的4,614例HFRS病例(历时13年)。基于既往空间研究将病例划分为四个区域,这些区域代表了不同的丘陵和平原地区,且与主要水体和山脉的 proximity 各不相同。HFRS病例数据由县级疾病预防控制中心工作人员使用国家标准化病例调查问卷收集。比较了临床严重程度和就医行为(医院级别、发病至就诊间隔)。结果:聚集区I的HFRS病例临床严重程度最高(重型占22.41%,危重型占6.65%),而聚集区II的病例则明显较轻(重型占2.62%,危重型占1.31%)。发病至就诊间隔中位数在聚集区II最长(5天),而其他区域为2–4天。医院选择存在差异:聚集区I主要使用二级医院(65.88%);聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院的使用上几乎持平;聚集区III和非聚集区倾向于选择更高级别医院。结论:研究结果证实,江西省虽然是一个混合流行疫源地,但在临床严重程度和就医行为方面表现出显著的空间异质性。这些发现强调了在HFRS预防和控制中需要采取因地制宜的区域性策略。 syndrome,HFRS)是一种由汉坦病毒(hantavirus,HVs)感染引起的鼠传人畜共患传染病。中国是全球HFRS负担最重的国家,占全球报告病例的90%以上。2004年至2019年间,中国共报告209,209例HFRS病例,病死率(case fatality rate,CFR)为0.89%。江西省是中国HFRS高发区,具有汉滩病毒(Hantaan virus,HTNV)和首尔病毒(Seoul virus,SEOV)共同流行的特征。2005年至2024年间,江西省累计报告近万例HFRS病例,病死率为1.1%,且疫情分布于全省90%以上的县区。既往空间流行病学研究已识别出江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区:聚集区I位于九岭山脉与鄱阳湖西侧之间的西北部区域,为历史高发区,年均发病率为12.10/10万;聚集区II和III分别位于鄱阳湖东侧和南侧及武夷山区域,发病率依次降低至4.20/10万和1.80/10万。然而,既往研究仅关注了发病率的空间分布格局,对于不同聚集区之间病例的临床严重程度是否存在差异,以及患者的就医行为是否受到区域特征的影晌,尚缺乏系统的比较研究。基于此,研究人员提出假设:高发区居民可能具有较短的发病至就诊间隔,且当地医疗机构积累了更丰富的诊疗经验;同时,受空间和环境异质性影响,不同区域的病毒型别构成和宿主携带率可能存在差异,进而导致人群临床严重程度的区域差异。为验证上述假设,研究人员开展了这项回顾性比较研究。 **二、研究设计与核心方法** 该研究依托中国法定传染病监测系统,利用国家标准化HFRS病例调查问卷,由县级疾病预防控制中心专业人员在病例报告后开展流行病学调查,收集病例的一般人口学特征、实验室诊断情况、临床严重程度及就医行为信息,必要时辅以电话访谈补充。研究期间为2011年至2023年,共报告7,172例HFRS病例。经排除缺乏标准化流行病学调查数据(2,374例,占33.10%)以及存在逻辑错误或关键信息缺失的病例后,最终纳入4,614例(占全部报告病例的64.33%)进行分析,其中聚集区I 2,320例、聚集区II 1,120例、聚集区III 542例、非聚集区632例。研究样本在性别、年龄和主要职业构成上与全部报告病例基本可比,且纳入与排除病例的年龄和性别分布相似,提示选择偏倚有限。统计分析采用Kruskal-Wallis H检验比较连续变量,采用卡方检验或Fisher精确检验比较分类变量,组间两两比较采用Bonferroni校正。为调整潜在混杂因素,分别以临床严重程度(轻/中型对比重/危重型)和医院级别(二级对比三级/三级+)为因变量构建两个多变量logistic回归模型,协变量包括聚集区、年龄、性别、职业和发病年份,报告校正优势比(adjusted odds ratio,aOR)及95%置信区间。所有统计分析使用R软件(版本4.3.0)完成,以P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。 **三、主要研究结果** **(一)病例一般特征** 2011年至2023年,江西省累计报告HFRS病例7,172例,累积发病率为1.64/10万,年报告发病率总体呈下降趋势,从2011年的1.24/10万波动下降至2023年的0.66/10万。各聚集区累积发病率差异显著,聚集区I、II、III分别为7.50/10万、3.27/10万和1.46/10万,而非聚集区仅为0.34/10万。纳入分析的4,614例病例中,男女性别比为2.09:1,四个区域间无显著差异。平均年龄为49±18岁。聚集区I中0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域(14.44%对比4.59%~6.46%),而41–60岁年龄组的比例则相反(37.20%对比46.25%~49.45%)。聚集区I学生比例显著高于其他区域,非聚集区农民比例显著低于其他区域。 **(二)临床严重程度分布** 在具有临床严重程度信息的4,403例病例中,轻型、中型、重型和危重型比例分别为49.15%、30.66%、15.17%和5.02%。聚集区II和非聚集区轻型病例比例较高,而聚集区I和III重型及危重型病例更为常见。聚集区I的危重型比例高于聚集区III。共记录79例死亡病例,总体病死率为1.79%。聚集区I(1.94%)和III(2.18%)的病死率相近,均高于聚集区II(0.47%)。值得注意的是,非聚集区的病死率最高,达3.31%。 **(三)就医行为** 在记录有就诊医院的4,533例病例中,0.55%前往一级医院就诊,51.36%前往二级医院,31.41%前往三级医院,16.68%前往三级+医院。聚集区I和II呈现从二级至三级+医院患者比例递减的趋势,而聚集区III和非聚集区则相反,其中非聚集区前往三级+医院就诊的比例最高(38.50%)。发病至就诊间隔分析在排除22例超过60天的记录错误后纳入4,592例。聚集区II的间隔中位数最长,为5天,显著长于聚集区I(3天)、聚集区III(2天)和非聚集区(4天)。这一模式在按性别、年龄和职业分层的亚组分析中保持一致。轻型病例的间隔中位数(4天)显著长于中型(3天)、重型(3天)和危重型(3天)。医院级别方面,三级医院病例的间隔最长(中位数4天),其次为二级(3天)、三级+(2天)和一级(1天)。 **(四)医院级别分布** 各聚集区的医院选择偏好差异显著。聚集区I以二级医院为主,占65.88%,仅19.17%前往三级医院。聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院之间呈近乎均衡的分布,且三级+医院就诊比例在所有区域中最低(3.31%)。相比之下,聚集区III和非聚集区前往三级+医院的比例大幅升高,分别为27.72%和38.50%。综合三级及三级+医院就诊比例,由高至低依次为:聚集区III(75.29%)、非聚集区(72.37%)、聚集区II(50.32%)和聚集区I(33.81%)。时间趋势分析显示,聚集区I-III的病例随时间推移越来越多地选择更高级别医院就诊。亚组分析显示,同区域内不同性别间医院级别分布相似(P=0.07)。各区域中,0–15岁年龄组前往三级/三级+医院的比例最高,且该比例随年龄增长而下降。农民前往三级/三级+医院的比例低于其他职业,而学生利用高级别医院的比例显著较高——尤其在聚集区III,92.59%的学生前往三级/三级+医院就诊。一级医院就诊仅见于轻型(0.56%)和中型(0.75%)病例,重型和危重型病例中完全没有。三级+医院就诊比例随疾病严重程度增加而上升,但轻型病例的该比例显著高于中型和重型。 **(五)实验室确认率** 各聚集区的实验室确认率差异显著。聚集区II在各严重程度类别中确认率均最低,而聚集区III在重型和危重型类别中确认率最高。不同医院级别间的确认率亦存在差异:聚集区I和III中三级+医院确认率最高,分别为79.82%和82.27%;非聚集区二级医院确认率最高(82.39%);聚集区II中二级(43.84%)和三级+(41.94%)确认率相当,均明显高于三级医院(25.30%)。 **(六)多变量回归分析** 以临床严重程度为因变量的logistic回归分析显示,与非聚集区病例相比,聚集区I和III患者发生重/危重病的风险显著增高,而聚集区II患者的风险显著降低。男性相对于女性重症风险增加22%。发病年份每增加1年,重症概率降低6%。年龄和职业亚类与严重程度无显著关联。以医院级别为因变量的回归分析显示,聚集区I和II患者在三级/三级+医院就诊的可能性较非聚集区显著降低,风险分别降低80%和58%。聚集区III呈正向趋势但未达统计学显著性。年龄增长与较低的三级/三级+入院概率相关,男性则高于女性。家务/失业及其他职业者比农民更有可能在三级/三级+医院就诊。发病年份每增加1年,三级医院入院概率增加4%。 **四、讨论与结论** 该研究首次聚焦江西省不同HFRS空间聚集区间的病例差异。聚集区I贡献了全省一半以上的报告病例,男女比例(2.09:1)低于相邻的浙江省(2.56:1)和湖北省(3:1),提示女性感染风险不容忽视。聚集区I的0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域而41–60岁年龄组偏低,研究人员推测前者与16岁以下人群未接种疫苗相关,后者可能与既往针对16–60岁人群的疫苗接种历史有关,但缺乏个体接种记录的直接支持。临床严重程度的显著区域差异可能归因于天然屏障(山脉和鄱阳湖)阻隔了宿主移动和病毒基因流动,以及海拔差异形成的生态位分化。实验室证据表明聚集区I某县仅存在HTNV而无SEOV,而聚集区II毗邻历史上HFRS流行的浙江省且两地SEOV毒株具有一定相似性。依据SEOV感染通常较HTNV感染临床表现更轻微这一既往文献证据,研究人员推测聚集区II可能以较温和的SEOV感染为主,而聚集区I则经历更高比例的HTNV相关重症,但这一基因型归属推断基于地理和文献线索而非本研究队列的直接病毒测序数据。非聚集区病死率最高可能与当地初级医疗机构对HFRS的诊疗意识有限以及转诊上级医院进行实验室确认所致的治疗延迟有关,该推测同样缺乏个体层面临床数据的直接支持。聚集区I和III严重程度分布相近可能与其地理邻近和共享主要啮齿动物宿主有关。发病至就诊间隔的区域差异与轻型病例比例、医疗可及性、交通基础设施和HFRS防治知识宣传程度等因素相关。聚集区I主要使用二级医院提示当地县级医院积累了较强的HFRS诊疗经验,而聚集区II的较低实验室确认率(34.96%对比69.79%)与较长就诊间隔相符,提示基层医院诊断能力不足可能导致转诊延迟。医院级别选择的职业分化可能反映社会经济地位差异:家务/失业者及其他职业者比农民更倾向于高等级医院,而学生与非农民无显著差异。 该研究存在以下局限:约33%的排除率可能引入选择偏倚,尽管纳入与排除病例的年龄性别分布相似,但重症患者可能因记录更完整而被优先保留,从而高估重/危重比例;各聚集区间排除率差异显著(15.79%~57.27%),排除率高的区域可能不成比例地遗漏轻型病例,干扰区域间比较;缺乏病毒基因分型数据(如HTNV对比SEOV)和个体接种记录,病毒和免疫机制的阐释属于推测性质;缺乏健康素养或医疗可及性的直接测量,以发病至就诊间隔和医院级别作为替代指标不可避免受到区域基础设施和卫生系统因素的混杂;13年回顾性数据无法确定就医行为与临床严重程度之间关联的方向性。 研究结论:该回顾性研究的发现为江西省HFRS严重程度和就医模式的区域异质性提供了探索性证据。与高发区被自然屏障隔离的聚集区II表现出较低的重症比例和较长的发病至就诊间隔,强调了实施地理差异化公共卫生策略的必要性。在重症聚集区(I和III),应优先加强预警系统和本地二级医院的重症监护能力;在轻型为主的聚集区(II),可考虑缩短发病至就诊间隔的干预措施,如社区健康教育、改善交通连接或加强基层转诊路径。在省级层面,观察到的异质性凸显了建立地理分层监测系统的重要性,以便及时发现新兴高风险区域并实现资源的适应性配置。需指出的是,这些政策建议属于假设生成性质,源于观察性关联而非已证实的因果机制。未来开展纳入病毒基因分型、健康素养评估和医疗可及性指标的前瞻性研究,对于验证这些观察结果和优化针对性干预措施十分必要。 virus,SEOV)共同流行的特征。2005年至2024年间,江西省累计报告近万例HFRS病例,病死率为1.1%,且疫情分布于全省90%以上的县区。既往空间流行病学研究已识别出江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区:聚集区I位于九岭山脉与鄱阳湖西侧之间的西北部区域,为历史高发区,年均发病率为12.10/10万;聚集区II和III分别位于鄱阳湖东侧和南侧及武夷山区域,发病率依次降低至4.20/10万和1.80/10万。然而,既往研究仅关注了发病率的空间分布格局,对于不同聚集区之间病例的临床严重程度是否存在差异,以及患者的就医行为是否受到区域特征的影晌,尚缺乏系统的比较研究。基于此,研究人员提出假设:高发区居民可能具有较短的发病至就诊间隔,且当地医疗机构积累了更丰富的诊疗经验;同时,受空间和环境异质性影响,不同区域的病毒型别构成和宿主携带率可能存在差异,进而导致人群临床严重程度的区域差异。为验证上述假设,研究人员开展了这项回顾性比较研究。**二、研究设计与核心方法**该研究依托中国法定传染病监测系统,利用国家标准化HFRS病例调查问卷,由县级疾病预防控制中心专业人员在病例报告后开展流行病学调查,收集病例的一般人口学特征、实验室诊断情况、临床严重程度及就医行为信息,必要时辅以电话访谈补充。研究期间为2011年至2023年,共报告7,172例HFRS病例。经排除缺乏标准化流行病学调查数据(2,374例,占33.10%)以及存在逻辑错误或关键信息缺失的病例后,最终纳入4,614例(占全部报告病例的64.33%)进行分析,其中聚集区I H检验比较连续变量,采用卡方检验或Fisher精确检验比较分类变量,组间两两比较采用Bonferroni校正。为调整潜在混杂因素,分别以临床严重程度(轻/中型对比重/危重型)和医院级别(二级对比三级/三级+)为因变量构建两个多变量logistic回归模型,协变量包括聚集区、年龄、性别、职业和发病年份,报告校正优势比(adjusted odds ratio,aOR)及95%置信区间。所有统计分析使用R软件(版本4.3.0)完成,以P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。**三、主要研究结果****(一)病例一般特征**2011年至2023年,江西省累计报告HFRS病例7,172例,累积发病率为1.64/10万,年报告发病率总体呈下降趋势,从2011年的1.24/10万波动下降至2023年的0.66/10万。各聚集区累积发病率差异显著,聚集区I、II、III分别为7.50/10万、3.27/10万和1.46/10万,而非聚集区仅为0.34/10万。纳入分析的4,614例病例中,男女性别比为2.09:1,四个区域间无显著差异。平均年龄为49±18岁。聚集区I中0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域(14.44%对比4.59%~6.46%),而41–60岁年龄组的比例则相反(37.20%对比46.25%~49.45%)。聚集区I学生比例显著高于其他区域,非聚集区农民比例显著低于其他区域。**(二)临床严重程度分布**在具有临床严重程度信息的4,403例病例中,轻型、中型、重型和危重型比例分别为49.15%、30.66%、15.17%和5.02%。聚集区II和非聚集区轻型病例比例较高,而聚集区I和III重型及危重型病例更为常见。聚集区I的危重型比例高于聚集区III。共记录79例死亡病例,总体病死率为1.79%。聚集区I(1.94%)和III(2.18%)的病死率相近,均高于聚集区II(0.47%)。值得注意的是,非聚集区的病死率最高,达3.31%。**(三)就医行为**在记录有就诊医院的4,533例病例中,0.55%前往一级医院就诊,51.36%前往二级医院,31.41%前往三级医院,16.68%前往三级+医院。聚集区I和II呈现从二级至三级+医院患者比例递减的趋势,而聚集区III和非聚集区则相反,其中非聚集区前往三级+医院就诊的比例最高(38.50%)。发病至就诊间隔分析在排除22例超过60天的记录错误后纳入4,592例。聚集区II的间隔中位数最长,为5天,显著长于聚集区I(3天)、聚集区III(2天)和非聚集区(4天)。这一模式在按性别、年龄和职业分层的亚组分析中保持一致。轻型病例的间隔中位数(4天)显著长于中型(3天)、重型(3天)和危重型(3天)。医院级别方面,三级医院病例的间隔最长(中位数4天),其次为二级(3天)、三级+(2天)和一级(1天)。**(四)医院级别分布**各聚集区的医院选择偏好差异显著。聚集区I以二级医院为主,占65.88%,仅19.17%前往三级医院。聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院之间呈近乎均衡的分布,且三级+医院就诊比例在所有区域中最低(3.31%)。相比之下,聚集区III和非聚集区前往三级+医院的比例大幅升高,分别为27.72%和38.50%。综合三级及三级+医院就诊比例,由高至低依次为:聚集区III(75.29%)、非聚集区(72.37%)、聚集区II(50.32%)和聚集区I(33.81%)。时间趋势分析显示,聚集区I-III的病例随时间推移越来越多地选择更高级别医院就诊。亚组分析显示,同区域内不同性别间医院级别分布相似(P=0.07)。各区域中,0–15岁年龄组前往三级/三级+医院的比例最高,且该比例随年龄增长而下降。农民前往三级/三级+医院的比例低于其他职业,而学生利用高级别医院的比例显著较高——尤其在聚集区III,92.59%的学生前往三级/三级+医院就诊。一级医院就诊仅见于轻型(0.56%)和中型(0.75%)病例,重型和危重型病例中完全没有。三级+医院就诊比例随疾病严重程度增加而上升,但轻型病例的该比例显著高于中型和重型。**(五)实验室确认率**各聚集区的实验室确认率差异显著。聚集区II在各严重程度类别中确认率均最低,而聚集区III在重型和危重型类别中确认率最高。不同医院级别间的确认率亦存在差异:聚集区I和III中三级+医院确认率最高,分别为79.82%和82.27%;非聚集区二级医院确认率最高(82.39%);聚集区II中二级(43.84%)和三级+(41.94%)确认率相当,均明显高于三级医院(25.30%)。**(六)多变量回归分析**以临床严重程度为因变量的logistic回归分析显示,与非聚集区病例相比,聚集区I和III患者发生重/危重病的风险显著增高,而聚集区II患者的风险显著降低。男性相对于女性重症风险增加22%。发病年份每增加1年,重症概率降低6%。年龄和职业亚类与严重程度无显著关联。以医院级别为因变量的回归分析显示,聚集区I和II患者在三级/三级+医院就诊的可能性较非聚集区显著降低,风险分别降低80%和58%。聚集区III呈正向趋势但未达统计学显著性。年龄增长与较低的三级/三级+入院概率相关,男性则高于女性。家务/失业及其他职业者比农民更有可能在三级/三级+医院就诊。发病年份每增加1年,三级医院入院概率增加4%。**四、讨论与结论**该研究首次聚焦江西省不同HFRS空间聚集区间的病例差异。聚集区I贡献了全省一半以上的报告病例,男女比例(2.09:1)低于相邻的浙江省(2.56:1)和湖北省(3:1),提示女性感染风险不容忽视。聚集区I的0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域而41–60岁年龄组偏低,研究人员推测前者与16岁以下人群未接种疫苗相关,后者可能与既往针对16–60岁人群的疫苗接种历史有关,但缺乏个体接种记录的直接支持。临床严重程度的显著区域差异可能归因于天然屏障(山脉和鄱阳湖)阻隔了宿主移动和病毒基因流动,以及海拔差异形成的生态位分化。实验室证据表明聚集区I某县仅存在HTNV而无SEOV,而聚集区II毗邻历史上HFRS流行的浙江省且两地SEOV毒株具有一定相似性。依据SEOV感染通常较HTNV感染临床表现更轻微这一既往文献证据,研究人员推测聚集区II可能以较温和的SEOV感染为主,而聚集区I则经历更高比例的HTNV相关重症,但这一基因型归属推断基于地理和文献线索而非本研究队列的直接病毒测序数据。非聚集区病死率最高可能与当地初级医疗机构对HFRS的诊疗意识有限以及转诊上级医院进行实验室确认所致的治疗延迟有关,该推测同样缺乏个体层面临床数据的直接支持。聚集区I和III严重程度分布相近可能与其地理邻近和共享主要啮齿动物宿主有关。发病至就诊间隔的区域差异与轻型病例比例、医疗可及性、交通基础设施和HFRS防治知识宣传程度等因素相关。聚集区I主要使用二级医院提示当地县级医院积累了较强的HFRS诊疗经验,而聚集区II的较低实验室确认率(34.96%对比69.79%)与较长就诊间隔相符,提示基层医院诊断能力不足可能导致转诊延迟。医院级别选择的职业分化可能反映社会经济地位差异:家务/失业者及其他职业者比农民更倾向于高等级医院,而学生与非农民无显著差异。该研究存在以下局限:约33%的排除率可能引入选择偏倚,尽管纳入与排除病例的年龄性别分布相似,但重症患者可能因记录更完整而被优先保留,从而高估重/危重比例;各聚集区间排除率差异显著(15.79%~57.27%),排除率高的区域可能不成比例地遗漏轻型病例,干扰区域间比较;缺乏病毒基因分型数据(如HTNV对比SEOV)和个体接种记录,病毒和免疫机制的阐释属于推测性质;缺乏健康素养或医疗可及性的直接测量,以发病至就诊间隔和医院级别作为替代指标不可避免受到区域基础设施和卫生系统因素的混杂;13年回顾性数据无法确定就医行为与临床严重程度之间关联的方向性。研究结论:该回顾性研究的发现为江西省HFRS严重程度和就医模式的区域异质性提供了探索性证据。与高发区被自然屏障隔离的聚集区II表现出较低的重症比例和较长的发病至就诊间隔,强调了实施地理差异化公共卫生策略的必要性。在重症聚集区(I和III),应优先加强预警系统和本地二级医院的重症监护能力;在轻型为主的聚集区(II),可考虑缩短发病至就诊间隔的干预措施,如社区健康教育、改善交通连接或加强基层转诊路径。在省级层面,观察到的异质性凸显了建立地理分层监测系统的重要性,以便及时发现新兴高风险区域并实现资源的适应性配置。需指出的是,这些政策建议属于假设生成性质,源于观察性关联而非已证实的因果机制。未来开展纳入病毒基因分型、健康素养评估和医疗可及性指标的前瞻性研究,对于验证这些观察结果和优化针对性干预措施十分必要。 摘要翻译:背景:肾综合征出血热(HFRS)是中国江西省的一项重大公共卫生问题,汉滩病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)在该地区共同流行。既往研究已确定江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区,其特点是地理分隔且发病率水平存在异质性。研究人员假设这些聚集区之间的临床严重程度和就医行为可能存在差异,并因此开展了一项回顾性研究以检验该假设。方法:研究人员回顾性分析了来自63个县的4,614例HFRS病例(历时13年)。基于既往空间研究将病例划分为四个区域,这些区域代表了不同的丘陵和平原地区,且与主要水体和山脉的 proximity 各不相同。HFRS病例数据由县级疾病预防控制中心工作人员使用国家标准化病例调查问卷收集。比较了临床严重程度和就医行为(医院级别、发病至就诊间隔)。结果:聚集区I的HFRS病例临床严重程度最高(重型占22.41%,危重型占6.65%),而聚集区II的病例则明显较轻(重型占2.62%,危重型占1.31%)。发病至就诊间隔中位数在聚集区II最长(5天),而其他区域为2–4天。医院选择存在差异:聚集区I主要使用二级医院(65.88%);聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院的使用上几乎持平;聚集区III和非聚集区倾向于选择更高级别医院。结论:研究结果证实,江西省虽然是一个混合流行疫源地,但在临床严重程度和就医行为方面表现出显著的空间异质性。这些发现强调了在HFRS预防和控制中需要采取因地制宜的区域性策略。 基于江西肾综合征出血热空间聚集区间的比较研究,现从学术评审角度对该论文主体内容进行系统解读与分析。 瑞孚迪多肽药物研发解决方案>> 领 取 **一、研究背景与问题的提出** 肾综合征出血热(hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,HFRS)是一种由汉坦病毒(hantavirus,HVs)感染引起的鼠传人畜共患传染病。中国是全球HFRS负担最重的国家,占全球报告病例的90%以上。2004年至2019年间,中国共报告209,209例HFRS病例,病死率(case fatality rate,CFR)为0.89%。江西省是中国HFRS高发区,具有汉滩病毒(Hantaan virus,HTNV)和首尔病毒(Seoul virus,SEOV)共同流行的特征。2005年至2024年间,江西省累计报告近万例HFRS病例,病死率为1.1%,且疫情分布于全省90%以上的县区。既往空间流行病学研究已识别出江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区:聚集区I位于九岭山脉与鄱阳湖西侧之间的西北部区域,为历史高发区,年均发病率为12.10/10万;聚集区II和III分别位于鄱阳湖东侧和南侧及武夷山区域,发病率依次降低至4.20/10万和1.80/10万。然而,既往研究仅关注了发病率的空间分布格局,对于不同聚集区之间病例的临床严重程度是否存在差异,以及患者的就医行为是否受到区域特征的影晌,尚缺乏系统的比较研究。基于此,研究人员提出假设:高发区居民可能具有较短的发病至就诊间隔,且当地医疗机构积累了更丰富的诊疗经验;同时,受空间和环境异质性影响,不同区域的病毒型别构成和宿主携带率可能存在差异,进而导致人群临床严重程度的区域差异。为验证上述假设,研究人员开展了这项回顾性比较研究。 **二、研究设计与核心方法** 该研究依托中国法定传染病监测系统,利用国家标准化HFRS病例调查问卷,由县级疾病预防控制中心专业人员在病例报告后开展流行病学调查,收集病例的一般人口学特征、实验室诊断情况、临床严重程度及就医行为信息,必要时辅以电话访谈补充。研究期间为2011年至2023年,共报告7,172例HFRS病例。经排除缺乏标准化流行病学调查数据(2,374例,占33.10%)以及存在逻辑错误或关键信息缺失的病例后,最终纳入4,614例(占全部报告病例的64.33%)进行分析,其中聚集区I 2,320例、聚集区II 1,120例、聚集区III 542例、非聚集区632例。研究样本在性别、年龄和主要职业构成上与全部报告病例基本可比,且纳入与排除病例的年龄和性别分布相似,提示选择偏倚有限。统计分析采用Kruskal-Wallis H检验比较连续变量,采用卡方检验或Fisher精确检验比较分类变量,组间两两比较采用Bonferroni校正。为调整潜在混杂因素,分别以临床严重程度(轻/中型对比重/危重型)和医院级别(二级对比三级/三级+)为因变量构建两个多变量logistic回归模型,协变量包括聚集区、年龄、性别、职业和发病年份,报告校正优势比(adjusted odds ratio,aOR)及95%置信区间。所有统计分析使用R软件(版本4.3.0)完成,以P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。 **三、主要研究结果** **(一)病例一般特征** 2011年至2023年,江西省累计报告HFRS病例7,172例,累积发病率为1.64/10万,年报告发病率总体呈下降趋势,从2011年的1.24/10万波动下降至2023年的0.66/10万。各聚集区累积发病率差异显著,聚集区I、II、III分别为7.50/10万、3.27/10万和1.46/10万,而非聚集区仅为0.34/10万。纳入分析的4,614例病例中,男女性别比为2.09:1,四个区域间无显著差异。平均年龄为49±18岁。聚集区I中0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域(14.44%对比4.59%~6.46%),而41–60岁年龄组的比例则相反(37.20%对比46.25%~49.45%)。聚集区I学生比例显著高于其他区域,非聚集区农民比例显著低于其他区域。 **(二)临床严重程度分布** 在具有临床严重程度信息的4,403例病例中,轻型、中型、重型和危重型比例分别为49.15%、30.66%、15.17%和5.02%。聚集区II和非聚集区轻型病例比例较高,而聚集区I和III重型及危重型病例更为常见。聚集区I的危重型比例高于聚集区III。共记录79例死亡病例,总体病死率为1.79%。聚集区I(1.94%)和III(2.18%)的病死率相近,均高于聚集区II(0.47%)。值得注意的是,非聚集区的病死率最高,达3.31%。 **(三)就医行为** 在记录有就诊医院的4,533例病例中,0.55%前往一级医院就诊,51.36%前往二级医院,31.41%前往三级医院,16.68%前往三级+医院。聚集区I和II呈现从二级至三级+医院患者比例递减的趋势,而聚集区III和非聚集区则相反,其中非聚集区前往三级+医院就诊的比例最高(38.50%)。发病至就诊间隔分析在排除22例超过60天的记录错误后纳入4,592例。聚集区II的间隔中位数最长,为5天,显著长于聚集区I(3天)、聚集区III(2天)和非聚集区(4天)。这一模式在按性别、年龄和职业分层的亚组分析中保持一致。轻型病例的间隔中位数(4天)显著长于中型(3天)、重型(3天)和危重型(3天)。医院级别方面,三级医院病例的间隔最长(中位数4天),其次为二级(3天)、三级+(2天)和一级(1天)。 **(四)医院级别分布** 各聚集区的医院选择偏好差异显著。聚集区I以二级医院为主,占65.88%,仅19.17%前往三级医院。聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院之间呈近乎均衡的分布,且三级+医院就诊比例在所有区域中最低(3.31%)。相比之下,聚集区III和非聚集区前往三级+医院的比例大幅升高,分别为27.72%和38.50%。综合三级及三级+医院就诊比例,由高至低依次为:聚集区III(75.29%)、非聚集区(72.37%)、聚集区II(50.32%)和聚集区I(33.81%)。时间趋势分析显示,聚集区I-III的病例随时间推移越来越多地选择更高级别医院就诊。亚组分析显示,同区域内不同性别间医院级别分布相似(P=0.07)。各区域中,0–15岁年龄组前往三级/三级+医院的比例最高,且该比例随年龄增长而下降。农民前往三级/三级+医院的比例低于其他职业,而学生利用高级别医院的比例显著较高——尤其在聚集区III,92.59%的学生前往三级/三级+医院就诊。一级医院就诊仅见于轻型(0.56%)和中型(0.75%)病例,重型和危重型病例中完全没有。三级+医院就诊比例随疾病严重程度增加而上升,但轻型病例的该比例显著高于中型和重型。 **(五)实验室确认率** 各聚集区的实验室确认率差异显著。聚集区II在各严重程度类别中确认率均最低,而聚集区III在重型和危重型类别中确认率最高。不同医院级别间的确认率亦存在差异:聚集区I和III中三级+医院确认率最高,分别为79.82%和82.27%;非聚集区二级医院确认率最高(82.39%);聚集区II中二级(43.84%)和三级+(41.94%)确认率相当,均明显高于三级医院(25.30%)。 **(六)多变量回归分析** 以临床严重程度为因变量的logistic回归分析显示,与非聚集区病例相比,聚集区I和III患者发生重/危重病的风险显著增高,而聚集区II患者的风险显著降低。男性相对于女性重症风险增加22%。发病年份每增加1年,重症概率降低6%。年龄和职业亚类与严重程度无显著关联。以医院级别为因变量的回归分析显示,聚集区I和II患者在三级/三级+医院就诊的可能性较非聚集区显著降低,风险分别降低80%和58%。聚集区III呈正向趋势但未达统计学显著性。年龄增长与较低的三级/三级+入院概率相关,男性则高于女性。家务/失业及其他职业者比农民更有可能在三级/三级+医院就诊。发病年份每增加1年,三级医院入院概率增加4%。 **四、讨论与结论** 该研究首次聚焦江西省不同HFRS空间聚集区间的病例差异。聚集区I贡献了全省一半以上的报告病例,男女比例(2.09:1)低于相邻的浙江省(2.56:1)和湖北省(3:1),提示女性感染风险不容忽视。聚集区I的0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域而41–60岁年龄组偏低,研究人员推测前者与16岁以下人群未接种疫苗相关,后者可能与既往针对16–60岁人群的疫苗接种历史有关,但缺乏个体接种记录的直接支持。临床严重程度的显著区域差异可能归因于天然屏障(山脉和鄱阳湖)阻隔了宿主移动和病毒基因流动,以及海拔差异形成的生态位分化。实验室证据表明聚集区I某县仅存在HTNV而无SEOV,而聚集区II毗邻历史上HFRS流行的浙江省且两地SEOV毒株具有一定相似性。依据SEOV感染通常较HTNV感染临床表现更轻微这一既往文献证据,研究人员推测聚集区II可能以较温和的SEOV感染为主,而聚集区I则经历更高比例的HTNV相关重症,但这一基因型归属推断基于地理和文献线索而非本研究队列的直接病毒测序数据。非聚集区病死率最高可能与当地初级医疗机构对HFRS的诊疗意识有限以及转诊上级医院进行实验室确认所致的治疗延迟有关,该推测同样缺乏个体层面临床数据的直接支持。聚集区I和III严重程度分布相近可能与其地理邻近和共享主要啮齿动物宿主有关。发病至就诊间隔的区域差异与轻型病例比例、医疗可及性、交通基础设施和HFRS防治知识宣传程度等因素相关。聚集区I主要使用二级医院提示当地县级医院积累了较强的HFRS诊疗经验,而聚集区II的较低实验室确认率(34.96%对比69.79%)与较长就诊间隔相符,提示基层医院诊断能力不足可能导致转诊延迟。医院级别选择的职业分化可能反映社会经济地位差异:家务/失业者及其他职业者比农民更倾向于高等级医院,而学生与非农民无显著差异。 该研究存在以下局限:约33%的排除率可能引入选择偏倚,尽管纳入与排除病例的年龄性别分布相似,但重症患者可能因记录更完整而被优先保留,从而高估重/危重比例;各聚集区间排除率差异显著(15.79%~57.27%),排除率高的区域可能不成比例地遗漏轻型病例,干扰区域间比较;缺乏病毒基因分型数据(如HTNV对比SEOV)和个体接种记录,病毒和免疫机制的阐释属于推测性质;缺乏健康素养或医疗可及性的直接测量,以发病至就诊间隔和医院级别作为替代指标不可避免受到区域基础设施和卫生系统因素的混杂;13年回顾性数据无法确定就医行为与临床严重程度之间关联的方向性。 研究结论:该回顾性研究的发现为江西省HFRS严重程度和就医模式的区域异质性提供了探索性证据。与高发区被自然屏障隔离的聚集区II表现出较低的重症比例和较长的发病至就诊间隔,强调了实施地理差异化公共卫生策略的必要性。在重症聚集区(I和III),应优先加强预警系统和本地二级医院的重症监护能力;在轻型为主的聚集区(II),可考虑缩短发病至就诊间隔的干预措施,如社区健康教育、改善交通连接或加强基层转诊路径。在省级层面,观察到的异质性凸显了建立地理分层监测系统的重要性,以便及时发现新兴高风险区域并实现资源的适应性配置。需指出的是,这些政策建议属于假设生成性质,源于观察性关联而非已证实的因果机制。未来开展纳入病毒基因分型、健康素养评估和医疗可及性指标的前瞻性研究,对于验证这些观察结果和优化针对性干预措施十分必要。 ratio,aOR)及95%置信区间。所有统计分析使用R软件(版本4.3.0)完成,以P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。**三、主要研究结果****(一)病例一般特征**2011年至2023年,江西省累计报告HFRS病例7,172例,累积发病率为1.64/10万,年报告发病率总体呈下降趋势,从2011年的1.24/10万波动下降至2023年的0.66/10万。各聚集区累积发病率差异显著,聚集区I、II、III分别为7.50/10万、3.27/10万和1.46/10万,而非聚集区仅为0.34/10万。纳入分析的4,614例病例中,男女性别比为2.09:1,四个区域间无显著差异。平均年龄为49±18岁。聚集区I中0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域(14.44%对比4.59%~6.46%),而41–60岁年龄组的比例则相反(37.20%对比46.25%~49.45%)。聚集区I学生比例显著高于其他区域,非聚集区农民比例显著低于其他区域。**(二)临床严重程度分布**在具有临床严重程度信息的4,403例病例中,轻型、中型、重型和危重型比例分别为49.15%、30.66%、15.17%和5.02%。聚集区II和非聚集区轻型病例比例较高,而聚集区I和III重型及危重型病例更为常见。聚集区I的危重型比例高于聚集区III。共记录79例死亡病例,总体病死率为1.79%。聚集区I(1.94%)和III(2.18%)的病死率相近,均高于聚集区II(0.47%)。值得注意的是,非聚集区的病死率最高,达3.31%。**(三)就医行为**在记录有就诊医院的4,533例病例中,0.55%前往一级医院就诊,51.36%前往二级医院,31.41%前往三级医院,16.68%前往三级+医院。聚集区I和II呈现从二级至三级+医院患者比例递减的趋势,而聚集区III和非聚集区则相反,其中非聚集区前往三级+医院就诊的比例最高(38.50%)。发病至就诊间隔分析在排除22例超过60天的记录错误后纳入4,592例。聚集区II的间隔中位数最长,为5天,显著长于聚集区I(3天)、聚集区III(2天)和非聚集区(4天)。这一模式在按性别、年龄和职业分层的亚组分析中保持一致。轻型病例的间隔中位数(4天)显著长于中型(3天)、重型(3天)和危重型(3天)。医院级别方面,三级医院病例的间隔最长(中位数4天),其次为二级(3天)、三级+(2天)和一级(1天)。**(四)医院级别分布**各聚集区的医院选择偏好差异显著。聚集区I以二级医院为主,占65.88%,仅19.17%前往三级医院。聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院之间呈近乎均衡的分布,且三级+医院就诊比例在所有区域中最低(3.31%)。相比之下,聚集区III和非聚集区前往三级+医院的比例大幅升高,分别为27.72%和38.50%。综合三级及三级+医院就诊比例,由高至低依次为:聚集区III(75.29%)、非聚集区(72.37%)、聚集区II(50.32%)和聚集区I(33.81%)。时间趋势分析显示,聚集区I-III的病例随时间推移越来越多地选择更高级别医院就诊。亚组分析显示,同区域内不同性别间医院级别分布相似(P=0.07)。各区域中,0–15岁年龄组前往三级/三级+医院的比例最高,且该比例随年龄增长而下降。农民前往三级/三级+医院的比例低于其他职业,而学生利用高级别医院的比例显著较高——尤其在聚集区III,92.59%的学生前往三级/三级+医院就诊。一级医院就诊仅见于轻型(0.56%)和中型(0.75%)病例,重型和危重型病例中完全没有。三级+医院就诊比例随疾病严重程度增加而上升,但轻型病例的该比例显著高于中型和重型。**(五)实验室确认率**各聚集区的实验室确认率差异显著。聚集区II在各严重程度类别中确认率均最低,而聚集区III在重型和危重型类别中确认率最高。不同医院级别间的确认率亦存在差异:聚集区I和III中三级+医院确认率最高,分别为79.82%和82.27%;非聚集区二级医院确认率最高(82.39%);聚集区II中二级(43.84%)和三级+(41.94%)确认率相当,均明显高于三级医院(25.30%)。**(六)多变量回归分析**以临床严重程度为因变量的logistic回归分析显示,与非聚集区病例相比,聚集区I和III患者发生重/危重病的风险显著增高,而聚集区II患者的风险显著降低。男性相对于女性重症风险增加22%。发病年份每增加1年,重症概率降低6%。年龄和职业亚类与严重程度无显著关联。以医院级别为因变量的回归分析显示,聚集区I和II患者在三级/三级+医院就诊的可能性较非聚集区显著降低,风险分别降低80%和58%。聚集区III呈正向趋势但未达统计学显著性。年龄增长与较低的三级/三级+入院概率相关,男性则高于女性。家务/失业及其他职业者比农民更有可能在三级/三级+医院就诊。发病年份每增加1年,三级医院入院概率增加4%。**四、讨论与结论**该研究首次聚焦江西省不同HFRS空间聚集区间的病例差异。聚集区I贡献了全省一半以上的报告病例,男女比例(2.09:1)低于相邻的浙江省(2.56:1)和湖北省(3:1),提示女性感染风险不容忽视。聚集区I的0–20岁年龄组比例显著高于其他区域而41–60岁年龄组偏低,研究人员推测前者与16岁以下人群未接种疫苗相关,后者可能与既往针对16–60岁人群的疫苗接种历史有关,但缺乏个体接种记录的直接支持。临床严重程度的显著区域差异可能归因于天然屏障(山脉和鄱阳湖)阻隔了宿主移动和病毒基因流动,以及海拔差异形成的生态位分化。实验室证据表明聚集区I某县仅存在HTNV而无SEOV,而聚集区II毗邻历史上HFRS流行的浙江省且两地SEOV毒株具有一定相似性。依据SEOV感染通常较HTNV感染临床表现更轻微这一既往文献证据,研究人员推测聚集区II可能以较温和的SEOV感染为主,而聚集区I则经历更高比例的HTNV相关重症,但这一基因型归属推断基于地理和文献线索而非本研究队列的直接病毒测序数据。非聚集区病死率最高可能与当地初级医疗机构对HFRS的诊疗意识有限以及转诊上级医院进行实验室确认所致的治疗延迟有关,该推测同样缺乏个体层面临床数据的直接支持。聚集区I和III严重程度分布相近可能与其地理邻近和共享主要啮齿动物宿主有关。发病至就诊间隔的区域差异与轻型病例比例、医疗可及性、交通基础设施和HFRS防治知识宣传程度等因素相关。聚集区I主要使用二级医院提示当地县级医院积累了较强的HFRS诊疗经验,而聚集区II的较低实验室确认率(34.96%对比69.79%)与较长就诊间隔相符,提示基层医院诊断能力不足可能导致转诊延迟。医院级别选择的职业分化可能反映社会经济地位差异:家务/失业者及其他职业者比农民更倾向于高等级医院,而学生与非农民无显著差异。该研究存在以下局限:约33%的排除率可能引入选择偏倚,尽管纳入与排除病例的年龄性别分布相似,但重症患者可能因记录更完整而被优先保留,从而高估重/危重比例;各聚集区间排除率差异显著(15.79%~57.27%),排除率高的区域可能不成比例地遗漏轻型病例,干扰区域间比较;缺乏病毒基因分型数据(如HTNV对比SEOV)和个体接种记录,病毒和免疫机制的阐释属于推测性质;缺乏健康素养或医疗可及性的直接测量,以发病至就诊间隔和医院级别作为替代指标不可避免受到区域基础设施和卫生系统因素的混杂;13年回顾性数据无法确定就医行为与临床严重程度之间关联的方向性。研究结论:该回顾性研究的发现为江西省HFRS严重程度和就医模式的区域异质性提供了探索性证据。与高发区被自然屏障隔离的聚集区II表现出较低的重症比例和较长的发病至就诊间隔,强调了实施地理差异化公共卫生策略的必要性。在重症聚集区(I和III),应优先加强预警系统和本地二级医院的重症监护能力;在轻型为主的聚集区(II),可考虑缩短发病至就诊间隔的干预措施,如社区健康教育、改善交通连接或加强基层转诊路径。在省级层面,观察到的异质性凸显了建立地理分层监测系统的重要性,以便及时发现新兴高风险区域并实现资源的适应性配置。需指出的是,这些政策建议属于假设生成性质,源于观察性关联而非已证实的因果机制。未来开展纳入病毒基因分型、健康素养评估和医疗可及性指标的前瞻性研究,对于验证这些观察结果和优化针对性干预措施十分必要。 source_language_evidence.event: 瑞孚迪多肽药物研发解决方案>> 领 取 **一、研究背景与问题的提出** 肾综合征出血热(hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,HFRS)是一种由汉坦病毒(hantavirus,HVs)感染引起的鼠传人畜共患传染病。中国是全球HFRS负担最重的国家,占全球报告病例的90%以上。2004年至2019年间,中国共报告209,209例HFRS病例,病死率(case fatality rate,CFR)为0.89%。江西省是中国HFRS高发区,具有汉滩病毒(Hantaan virus,HTNV)和首尔病毒(Seoul virus,SEOV)共同流行的特征。2005年至2024年间,江西省累计报告近万例HFRS病例,病死率为1.1%,且疫情分布于全省90%以上的县区。既往空间流行病学研究已识别出江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区:聚集区I位于九岭山脉与鄱阳湖西侧之间的西北部区域,为历史高发区,年均发病率为12.10/10万;聚集区II和III分别位于鄱阳湖东侧和南侧及武夷山区域,发病率依次降低至4.20/10万和1.80/10万。然而,既往研究仅关注了发病率的空间分布格局,对于不同聚集区之间病例的临床严重程度是否存在差异,以及患者的就医行为是否受到区域特征的影晌,尚缺乏系统的比较研究。基于此,研究人员提出假设:高发区居民可能具有较短的发病至就诊间隔,且当地医疗机构积累了更丰富的诊疗经验;同时,受空间和环境异质性影响,不同区域的病毒型别构成和宿主携带率可能存在差异,进而导致人群临床严重程度的区域差异。为验证上述假设,研究人员开展了这项回顾性比较研究。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: **(五)实验室确认率** 各聚集区的实验室确认率差异显著。聚集区II在各严重程度类别中确认率均最低,而聚集区III在重型和危重型类别中确认率最高。不同医院级别间的确认率亦存在差异:聚集区I和III中三级+医院确认率最高,分别为79.82%和82.27%;非聚集区二级医院确认率最高(82.39%);聚集区II中二级(43.84%)和三级+(41.94%)确认率相当,均明显高于三级医院(25.30%)。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 肾综合征出血热病例的临床严重程度与就医行为:中国江西省空间聚集区间的比较研究 《PLOS Pathogens》:Clinical severity and health-seeking behaviors of cases with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome: A comparative study across spatial clusters in Jiangxi Province, China 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年09月24日 来源:PLOS Pathogens 4.9 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article Open Access 摘要翻译:背景:肾综合征出血热(HFRS)是中国江西省的一项重大公共卫生问题,汉滩病毒(HTNV)和首尔病毒(SEOV)在该地区共同流行。既往研究已确定江西省存在三个特征鲜明的HFRS流行聚集区,其特点是地理分隔且发病率水平存在异质性。研究人员假设这些聚集区之间的临床严重程度和就医行为可能存在差异,并因此开展了一项回顾性研究以检验该假设。方法:研究人员回顾性分析了来自63个县的4,614例HFRS病例(历时13年)。基于既往空间研究将病例划分为四个区域,这些区域代表了不同的丘陵和平原地区,且与主要水体和山脉的 proximity 各不相同。HFRS病例数据由县级疾病预防控制中心工作人员使用国家标准化病例调查问卷收集。比较了临床严重程度和就医行为(医院级别、发病至就诊间隔)。结果:聚集区I的HFRS病例临床严重程度最高(重型占22.41%,危重型占6.65%),而聚集区II的病例则明显较轻(重型占2.62%,危重型占1.31%)。发病至就诊间隔中位数在聚集区II最长(5天),而其他区域为2–4天。医院选择存在差异:聚集区I主要使用二级医院(65.88%);聚集区II在二级(48.44%)和三级(47.01%)医院的使用上几乎持平;聚集区III和非聚集区倾向于选择更高级别医院。结论:研究结果证实,江西省虽然是一个混合流行疫源地,但在临床严重程度和就医行为方面表现出显著的空间异质性。这些发现强调了在HFRS预防和控制中需要采取因地制宜的区域性策略。 基于江西肾综合征出血热空间聚集区间的比较研究,现从学术评审角度对该论文主体内容进行系统解读与分析。 瑞孚迪多肽药物研发解决方案>> 领 取 **一、研究背景与问题的提出** 肾综合征出血热(hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,HFRS)是一种由汉坦病毒(hantavirus,HVs)感染引起的鼠传人畜共患传染病。中国是全球HFRS负担最重的国家,占全球报告病例的。
